documents.content:
Good morning.

Thank you. Good to be here. So, my name is Steve Jobs. I'm the interim CEO of Apple. And we get to spend a little bit of time this morning. I've got four things that I'd like to talk about, if that's okay. So let's get started. Of course, the first one, the first one is our new Power Macintosh G3. I hope all of you've seen this by now. And I want to tell you some of the thinking that went into designing this. We had four goals for the product. The first was to be the most powerful Macintosh ever designed, and even beyond that, the most powerful PC ever, of any kind. The second goal was to have the best graphics in the industry, including the best real-time 3D graphics. The third goal was to be the most expandable personal computer ever made. And the fourth fourth goal was to have the best design of any personal computer. So let's go through these goals one by one. The first one, the most powerful. How did we do it? Well, these G3 ship with a four up to a 400 MHz Power PC processor. And this is the first processor ever to ship commercially using copper. So it's very, very fast. And let's see how fast. Well, in addition to the processor running at 400 MHz, we've got the cache is running at 200 MHz and the memory running at 100 MHz. And so when we compare these to the fastest Pentium 2 money can buy, the 450 MHz, right? In byte marks, that's 5.6. The old G3s did 11.3, and the new G3s do over 13 byte marks. So these are really, really fast boxes. And to give you a demonstration of how fast, I'd like Phil Schiller, our worldwide vice president of product marketing, to join me, and we're going to do a bake off.

Phil, where's Phil?

I need Phil. All right, Dave. Come on.

Thanks for joining. Okay, what have we got here, Phil?

And the demo we're going to show you today is of Adobe Photoshop, one of the most used applications in the professional market. And we've got a large Photoshop file created by one of our customers. And this is a real file that was created to do a real job. Now how big is the file, Phil?

And we're going to have the fastest PC money can buy and the new Power Mac G3 step through these things as fast as they can and see which one is the fastest. Now this is exactly the same file running on both computers. So let's go.

Select Photoshop here. Okay, ready to go?

I'll count us down. Three, two, one, go. Okay, there goes the Mac is off. The PC is thinking, thinking. The deep thinker. So here we go. You might begin to guess what this algorithm is from. And the Macintosh is done.

We're getting there.

Okay. Now, one of the things, let's run this again, Phil. Uh one of the things that graphic artists do a lot in Photoshop is they revert. So let's even measure the revert time.

Three, two, one, revert.

Now the Macintosh is giving us status here, it's it's reverting. The PC is just uh

Getting an hourglass. And uh the Macintosh is ready again. The PC is thinking. And thinking some more. Okay, there we go. So let's run this test again. Uh I'll count down. Three, two, one, go. I didn't push it. I'm giving him a head start. Okay, now, the Macintosh is done now.

We're ahead of him already.

Uh-huh. Exactly what it means. And the Mac is done.

So what we're seeing here is that the PC is 62% slower than the Macintosh, running Photoshop exactly the same file, the kind of things that our customers do every single day, many, many times per day. Thank you, Phil.

Okay. So we've made the most powerful PC that you can buy. The best graphics. Now, Macintosh has always had great 2D graphics, but we wanted to go and extend that to 3D graphics. And we bet on a new technology that was going to come out about the same time as the G3. And that technology is the ATI Rage 128 graphics accelerator. It's the fastest graphics accelerator ever made for a personal computer. And Macintosh is the first and so far only PC to use it. We've complemented it with 16 megabytes of graphics memory. So it's very, very fast and it can store large texture maps. Now, a lot of different markets need 3D graphics: education, science, websites, business. But the one thing that pushes 3D graphics the hardest is games. Games not only push the 3D graphics the hardest, but they also push the whole system performance the hardest. And so I'd like to show you how fast this really is. Now, in the PC market, none of the PC manufacturers build in good 3D graphics. So to get good 3D graphics, you have to add an add-in card. And the most popular one and the best one in the PC market is the Voodoo 2 card. And it costs an extra, thank you. It costs an extra $200. What we're going to do is take a look at what the graphics built in to every new Power Mac G3, how does that compare with even this extra $200 card? Well, the graphics from the prior generation G3 used a chip called the Rage Pro. And it would play the game Quake at 36 frames per second. The Voodoo 2 card running in a PC, a 450 MHz Pentium 2 PC, would run Quake at 50 frames per second. The new ATI Rage 128 built into every G3 model for no extra charge runs Quake at 68 frames per second. So what I would love to do now is show you that. So can I get Phil back out here? Okay.

So Phil, what have we got here?

Great. And we've got a new great game here called Dark Vengeance, one of the hottest new 3D games. And what we're going to do is we're going to run Dark Vengeance on both machines at the same time. And there's a sequence of of play events that this game is going to go through, and we're going to see which one gets done quickest.

You like to count us down to begin?

Three, two, one, go.

Now, it turns out that the Mac was able to render that game at 55 frames per second versus 45 frames per second on the fastest PC with a $200 Voodoo 2 add-in card. So you can see the difference in performance there. The Mac is 20% faster than even the Voodoo 2 card added into the fastest PC. Thank you, Phil.

Now, now that we've got the best hardware in the industry, we wanted to provide a graphics library, a 3D graphics standard in software for our developers. And we chose what we think is the best one out there after talking with our developers, which is OpenGL from Silicon Graphics. And we've licensed that, and we're going to be building OpenGL into all future releases of the Macintosh operating system. And I think the game developers are extremely excited about this. So, we think we've nailed the best graphics in the industry. The most expandable. Well, to start with, you can add up to a gigabyte of memory inside our new Power Mac G3s. And you can add 100 gigabytes of disk inside that box using three disk drives. We can hold up to three disk drives, and we will be shipping the new IBM 36 gig disk drives as our highest end build to order option. So you can have over 100 gigabytes of disk drives inside the box with these three drives. In addition to that, we've added a fourth slot. So there are now four slots inside, and three of them are 64-bit PCI for very, very fast peripherals. On the IO ports, let me explain our philosophy first. We believe in using industry standards. We believe in using IO that is serial versus parallel, because high-speed serial IO means much smaller cables, much nicer for consumers as well as professionals. And we believe in plug and play. You should be able to plug it together and it should just work. No switches to set or anything else. So what IO have we built in to the new Power Mac G3 that meets this philosophy? Well, of course, the first one is Ethernet. Ethernet is an industry standard. It is high-speed serial interface. And we have 100 megabit Ethernet built in, and you can get it now with gigabit Ethernet available in the new Power Mac G3, the first personal computer in the industry to offer it. The second thing we've built in is Universal Serial Bus. This is a new industry standard that is terrific. It's called USB for short, and this is its symbol. Now, what does USB do that the old serial ports in the Mac didn't do? A lot. Let me compare them. The old serial ports ran fairly slow. USB is 30 times faster at 12 megabits per second. The serial ports, you could connect two devices to your Mac. With USB, you can connect 127 devices to your Macintosh. The old serial ports were not hot pluggable. You needed to really turn off the power to do something safe with. USB, you can plug in and out with the power on and it automatically self-configures. And the drivers are dynamically loadable. So when you plug in a new USB device, the drivers will be dynamically loaded in. And it's an industry standard, which means that when a peripheral company wants to make a new peripheral, to make a version for the Mac, all they have to do is write the driver. The hardware is exactly the same as what they would use for Windows. So this is really great. And the number of USB devices is going through the roof. **[Audience]**: [Applause]

**Ben Waldman**: Now, Steve has shown us that computer hardware can have style, it can be elegant. And at Microsoft, we also think that software should have style. documents.speaker: Steve Jobs
documents.content:
We have some great stuff this morning.

Uh, I hope you're pleased. It's going to be a long show. So I hope we keep you glued to your seats for a while. Okay, let's get started. For the last two years, we've been reinventing Apple. We've reinvented almost everything about the way we run our business, about the way we market our products, about the way we distribute our products, about the way we engineer our products. And it's been a lot of work by a lot of folks at Apple. We've had an incredibly loyal customer base that's stuck by us. And where we find ourselves today after this process is with the strongest product line in Apple's history. And last quarter, we filled out our product matrix with our last product, the iBook. And last quarter, for the first time, we were firing on all cylinders. And I've got some great news to tell you about last quarter. I'm going to we're going to save most of it for our earnings call two weeks from today. But one thing I want to share with you is that we have a reason to celebrate.

Um, because last quarter, we sold over 1,350,000 Macintoshes.

Incredible. That that is more Macs in one quarter than in any quarter in Apple's entire history.

1,350,000 is one Mac every six seconds of every minute of every hour of every day in the quarter. And a lot of people worked really hard uh in our operations team to make that happen and uh in our engineering teams as well. So uh congratulations everybody. Uh I think the team did a great job.

And the greatest thanks go to the Mac community for really believing with us, sticking with us, believing in us and uh and buying these great new products. So thank you very, very much. So, this is our product line today. I just want to review a few things about each product with you. Uh obviously our our pro desktop is our Power Mac G4. It's the fastest Macintosh we've ever built. At its heart, it's got a G4 chip with a velocity engine. The velocity engine brings supercomputer performance right to the personal computer desktop and it's incredible. Uh we also have, of course, the incredible packaging where you can get to any part inside in a matter of a few seconds. There's nothing else like it on the market. And we recently started shipping our new Cinema Display. This is our 22-inch LCD display that goes with the G4. It is the largest LCD display ever brought to market. It is the finest computer display in the world. And when you pair it up with the G4, we have got the hottest pro desktop lineup on the planet. So that is our Power Mac G4. Portables, our portables did fantastic last quarter. Last quarter, our two portables, our iBooks and our PowerBooks, garnered an 11% market share in the month of November, which is the latest data we have, the most recent data, an 11% share of the US retail and mail order market. That is as large as the that's larger than Apple's portable market share has been in years. And of course, the volume was led by the iBook. The iBook has been a runaway success for us. And in the months of October and November, which are the most recent data we've got, iBook was the number one selling consumer portable in the US.

Now, we do a lot of market research to find out who's buying our products and why and what problems they may be having with them. So I've got some to share with you that's really interesting. First-time buyers of iBooks, 11%, right? So most of them already own a computer, obviously. But Wintel switchers, 17%.

Which means which means that 28% of iMac buyers are new customers to Apple, which is great. Now, first portable in the home, over half. So we really have built the first true consumer portable. No other portable has statistics like this. The first true consumer portable rather than yesterday's business portable warmed up for consumers. 16% have already installed Airport in the first few months of the life of the product. That's one out of every six iBook owners is already installed Airport. We're really happy about that. 90% of these folks are on the internet. Again, one out of six of them wirelessly. 90% on the internet and 70% have already purchased goods and services over the internet. So we're extraordinarily pleased with these numbers, our first quarter of iBook sales that we have market research on. So iBook has been a huge success. We could not be happier uh with our portable product line right now. Which brings us to, of course, iMac. The new iMac started shipping last quarter and these are incredible products. I I am so proud of the team uh that engineered this product. It is phenomenally good. It is one of my favorites. And uh of course, they come in the five colors, but we also broke it down into three product options: the $9.95 iMac, the $12.99 iMac DV, and the $14.99 iMac DV Special Edition. And what happened last quarter was the Special Edition was the hit among the three hits. And we couldn't even make enough. We shipped a lot of Special Editions, but it wasn't enough and uh this product took off like a rocket. We have some market research on the iMacs. Who's buying them? 30% first-time buyers, 14% Wintel switchers, which means that 44% of iMac customers are new customers.

documents.content:
7 gigaflops. And we want to get this performance out to everybody. So, as you know, we make three models of Power Max. And what we're going to do is take the 400 megahertz model and keep it a single processor, but we've now made the 450 and the 500 megahertz models dual processor standard, built in standard. You can't even buy them with one processor anymore.

And these are incredible machines. We've gone even further. We've built in gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard now. It does not even take a slot. So you have gigabit Ethernet built into every one of these three Power Mac models. We've also increased the mass storage to 20, 30 and 40 gigabytes. We've included the new optical mouse and pro keyboard, and these incredible machines with all of this are the same price as before. So,

This is what we've been up to with the Power Mac G4. And uh again, based on this incredible G4 chip, two brains are better than one. So we're going dual processor in the two high-end models, Power Mac G4. Now, we have something new on the G4 today. The G4 ships with uh pretty fast 3D graphics. Rage 128 Pro chip is standard. But today we're introducing what many believe to be the fastest graphics chip in the land, which is the new ATI Radeon graphics chip.

The the ATI Radeon is over twice as fast as the Rage 128 Pro, and it's going to be $100 extra if you order a computer on the Apple online store. $100 extra for the Radeon. And uh we have a demonstration to show you right now. Phil, let's give him a demo of the Radeon versus the Rage 128.

I'm really excited to be able to show this to all of you today for the first time. This is the first time we get to show this, a Power Mac with a brand new Radeon graphics chip in it. What we have up on the screen are two Power Macs that are almost identical. They have the same processors, same memory, same discs. There's just one small difference. The Power Mac on your left has the Rage 128 Pro, and the Power Mac on your right has the brand new Radeon card in it. Now, we're going to do a demonstration using Quake 3 Arena from Id Software. A lot of you know Quake 3D, Quake 3 Arena because it is an OpenGL application. In fact, it is the most popular OpenGL application in the world, and as such, really can exercise 3D graphics and take maximum advantage of all this new hardware performance. And with this demo, we can go through a script that will run through as fast as it can on both machines to see whoever gets done first is fastest. Now, some of you may not like violent game demos, so if you if you don't, you can certainly choose not to watch. Um but I promise you that uh no humans were used in running the software. Uh no humans were injured in this test. So Steve, if you can help me, select the demo.

And we'll on the count of three, click play. 3, 2, 1, go. And this is going to run through every single frame on both machines as fast as it can.

So far, loading the same time. It's using the hard drive, the same hard drives.

Let's let it run all the way through.

Now it's still finishing on the left.

Ooh.

So, what many believe to be the fastest graphics chip now available is shipping, is going to ship starting today in volume uh on any Power Mac G4, order it at the Apple store, $100 extra, Radeon graphics. So that is what's up with the Power Mac G4. Next, we introduced the Power Mac G4 Cube. An incredible new product from Apple. It's a Power Mac through and through. The nickname we call it is the G4 Cube. And this thing's remarkable. We have taken an entire Power Mac and shrunk it down into a tiny little cube that's 20 centimeters on a side. Less than 8 inches on a side. Right? Power Mac G4 Cube. If you want to see how big this is relative to a tower, this is the Power Mac G4 tower. This is the cube. And yet it has the same power inside it. We also built in a DVD drive right in the top there. You can see. It's kind of cute. Whoops, there we go. You know. And um the other thing that's remarkable about this is normally it would take a giant fan to cool all this power in such a tiny space. But again, our engineering team did some brilliant work and figured out how to cool it with a brilliant air convection system that does not require a fan. And so the G4 Cube runs virtually silent right on your desktop. It's amazing. Inside this box is a G4 chip, up to a gigabyte and a half of memory. You can configure it up to a 40 gigabyte disc drive. It's got all the IO you'd ever want, built in modem, built in Ethernet, USB and firewire. It's got fast graphics or faster graphics if you want to order it, BTO with a Radeon card. And optionally, it has airport wireless networking and the antennas are built into every cube, so it's ready for an airport card if you want to drop one in. And the cube comes standard not only with the new optical mouse and keyboard, but a set of beautiful uh Apple designed Harmon Cardon speakers. These things sound fantastic. This comes standard with this stuff in this configuration, a 450 megahertz G4, 64 mega memory, 20 gigabytes of storage, Rage 128 graphics, a DVD, of course, firewire and iMovie for $1799. And in the local currencies here, these are the prices.

So, we're very happy with this. We also introduced some new displays. We have three basically new displays. All these displays connect to the cube and now to the tower as well with one cable. And this one universal cable carries video, both analog and digital. It carries USB and it carries power. So these new displays are actually powered from the computers. You don't have to have a separate cord to plug them in. We have a new 17-inch CRT. It's a flat diamatron. It's very nice. It's got two USB ports built in. It's got color sync built in and it's powered from the computer. One cable going back to the computer. Second display is a new 15-inch flat LCD. This is very, very sweet. It's 10x7 resolution. It has two USB ports. It has touch controls on it to adjust it and it is also powered from the computer. It makes a phenomenally nice match with the G4 Cube. Really beautiful. And we have a new version of the cinema display that again has that one universal connector to connect it to the tower or the cube and you don't need a separate power supply. So three new displays. Now I've got a video I'd like to show you so you can get a really good look at what the cube looks like and I'd like to roll that right now.

In first grade when I was painting with poster paints, I painted a boat and I made the smoke go in the right direction and my first grade teacher told my mom, you should nurture his artistic ability. I've been a visual person ever since. Uh I was an art director, I'm a designer and I just love how the cube looks. I mean, it's just the coolest looking computer on the planet.

The first reaction I had to the size of the G4 Cube was really one of amazement because if you had asked me in advance how small can a supercomputer be, uh I never would have come close to what I saw.

3 and a half gigaflops. Now that is 3 and a half billion operations per second. Um it is staggering by any measure and 10 years ago it was unheard of in anything smaller than a washing machine.

The heart of the G4 Cube is incredibly complex. I mean it's it's a supercomputer. But we were looking for a fine design that was very simple. A design that left you with a sense of well of course that's the most natural, the most elegant solution possible.

All the kind of functional characteristics are taken care of, but then there's another level of aesthetic that just lifts it and gives it spirit.

Most computer companies would have said this is an impossible task. They would have walked away from it. I mean to take a computer four times its size and pack it down into an 8-inch cube, it seems impossible, but we did it. Being this big and being able to sustain one, two, three or four gigaflops. We are looking at 2,000 times the volume efficiency of say a Cray supercomputer of the 1980s. The G4 Cube starts out with 64 megabytes of memory, expandable up to 1.5 gigabytes of RAM. It starts with a 20 gigabyte hard drive, configurable up to 40 gigabytes. It's got all the IO you could ever want. Ethernet, USB, firewire, everything you need is in the cube. The W uses is going to love it. Um it has everything they require. It has the power of a G4, but it has the elegance and the design element that they care about. The G4 Cube is designed to go onto your desk. So we saw that it was crucial that we could remove both visual and audible clutter. So the team figured out a way to actually remove the fan. The product's air cooled so that it's virtually silent. Instead of sitting down at a computer that's humming and and uh and you kind of feel technology in the room, you're sitting down in the silence where you can sit and have an idea. The DVD has a nice element of surprise in the way that it rises from the top of the cube, just like magic. You flip it over, there's this little latch that you hit and it pops up and you can pull the entire core out and almost looks like this nuclear reactor core, you know, something that you'd see in in Mission Impossible. There's easy access to all the RAM, uh to the airport cards, to the graphics cards. You don't have to then say, gee, I'm going to upgrade the memory, uh what expert am I going to have to find? Uh it's something that really an 8-year-old can do in in about 15 seconds. Along with this amazing little cube, you have a new keyboard, a professional new mouse. It's optical, so there's nothing to clog or jam. We reduced the speakers to an elemental form, the sphere. They're elegant, very simple and they sound they sound outrageous.

I love the new flat panel display. I just think both the big one and the smaller one are just the most beautiful things. Other people are totally in love with the way the new CRT looks. That see through back end is it's just so Apple. The new G4 Cube is the ultimate desktop movie making machine. It comes with iMovie 2 software. Or if you're a professional, you can step right up to Final Cut Pro. You get an idea, you walk out, you film it, you bring it back, you download it through firewire. You can play with it in Final Cut Pro, you know, add type, whatever and boom, it's done. Whether you do publishing, web design, video editing, this machine was made for you.

If I had only seen the Power Mac G4 Cube, I would have been very impressed. I would have said this is going to be a very important product for Apple and for users. Uh but it it didn't stop there and from from one experience to the next, uh it just kept getting better and better and I left kind of scratching my head thinking is is there anything that's missing from this product offering and uh I'm still thinking because I don't think there is.

I think the thing that I I'm most thrilled with is that the products are, I mean they are very different, but that together they do relate as as one very harmonious family.

Steve loves doing tada. And pulling the the sheet off of stuff and it was just another one of those tadas where you go, holy shit, they've done it again.

I think the G4 Cube may be the most incredible product Apple has ever engineered. And uh if you haven't seen one in person, I would uh suggest that it's a great opportunity over at the Expo to go actually see one and sit down and test drive it. It's a remarkable, remarkable Macintosh. Now, we've just finished uh creating two TV commercials that I would love to get your opinion on. I I would love to know which one you like better. And if you like them at all. Uh so I'm going to run them and uh I'd like you to tell me uh based on your applause which uh which one you you like. So there's two of them. Let's run the first one.

A super fast, super quiet, super computer in an 8 inch cube.

That's one.

Okay, let's run the second one.

According to quantum theory, tremendous energy can be compressed into a tiny packet. A tiny packet, indeed, presenting a supercomputer in an 8 inch cube.

Good. Well, we'll run them then. Okay. So, this is the new G4 Cube. And again, these three new desktop products, all new models. Everything less than eight weeks ago. So, this was our product line as of eight weeks ago. Uh but I have something new for you today in the iBook space.

iBook has been a wonderful product. It's been very successful and uh people love their iBooks. And so we've got today some new iBooks. So let's let's start with iBook. What was the number one requested feature of iBook?

Right. Number one requested feature is firewire and iMovie. And so all the new iBooks include firewire and iMovie 2. Now, we couldn't uh we couldn't rev the products without also revving the colors. So, we have two new colors for the iBook uh regular edition today and the first is Indigo and I'd love to show you right now. Indigo.

They're really, really good.
So this is our product line.
We're really happy with it.
I think it's the strongest product line that Apple has ever had.
Now I'd like to switch gears.
I'd like to talk about software.
The first thing I'd like to talk about is a really great app that's coming out that runs on all our products and that is the new Microsoft Office 2001.
And for the first public demo.

Yeah.
It's really good.
And for the first matter of fact, isn't it great that the Mac is going to have the best version of Office?
You know?

There's a team.
There's a team of a few hundred people at Microsoft who love the Mac.
And they work night and day to make the version of stuff on the Mac better than their colleagues in the rest of the company.

Now, we need to help these guys because as you can imagine, they don't get a lot of pats on the back in the lunchroom.
So, we they depend on us to give them some positive feedback so that when they go back to Redmond and tell everybody that the best version of Office now runs on the Mac, you know, they can have a little enthusiasm.
So please give a warm welcome to Kevin Brown, the general manager of the Mac business unit.
He's going to show us.

Thank you, Kevin.
Kevin and his team are doing a great job up in Redmond and we're working very closely with them on Office and on Internet Explorer and some other stuff and it's it's great.
So, Office 2001 coming in a few months here.
Now, brings us to Mac OS 10.

Mac OS 10 is the future of the Macintosh.
And it's turned out incredible.
We're not done yet.
We won't ship a final version till early next year, but we're very far along.
The rollout schedule for Mac OS 10 is as follows.
We announced it this last January.
We shipped a preview of it to our developers in February, another preview in May.
This summer we said we would have a public beta and we're going to release in early 2001.
Focusing on the summer public beta, we're going to release that today.

The public beta, the public beta is in English, French and German.

All of those languages, all of those languages are on one CD ROM, but we have three separate packages because of a little manual inside.
And we've held this in our hands for a long time.
Starting today, we're going to let you hold it in yours.
This is what it looks like.
There's a disc inside.
It's a little booklet to get you started.
Mac OS 10.

We have to print these things up and ship them around, so we're going to charge a nominal fee of 29.99 in the US or these prices local over here for it.
You can try it out.
And you can purchase it on any one of our web stores again in any of the countries.
You can also purchase it at the exhibit hall in our booth today.

So I'd like to go through the architecture of Mac OS 10.
We start with Darwin.
Darwin is the foundation kernel.
It's got all of the multi threading, the multi processing, the protected memory, the modern networking, all of the super modern plumbing that we wanted to put into Mac OS 10.
And it's based on the Mach 3 micro kernel and free BSD Unix.
So it's very, very open.
Matter of fact, it's so open, we've made it open source.
So you can go and download the whole source code to Darwin.
Tens of thousands of developers have already done so and we have an active community helping us ensure that Darwin is the most stable, reliable, highest performance kernel out there.
Now, on top of Darwin, we've layered some incredible new graphics technology.
Quartz, our 2D graphics is PDF based.
Adobe defined a specification for PDF which we have implemented our own version of, which is fantastic.
As you know, and the publishing industry is moving to PDF workflows, PDF is the standard on the web for high quality graphics and it is now built in as the primary 2D layer in the Macintosh operating system in Mac OS 10.
We've added transparency and some other great effects which you'll see in a minute.
We've built in OpenGL for 3D graphics and of course QuickTime for media.
All built into Mac OS 10 at a fundamental level.
On top of this, we've layered three APIs.
Classic lets you run existing Mac apps without modification.
However, you do not get advantage you do not get all the new features.
You do not get the new user interface, you do not get protected memory.
If one classic app crashes, all the classic apps that you may be running at that time will probably crash.
But you can run your existing apps without modification.
Now, the next API is carbon.
Carbon is something that takes developers a few months to tune up their classic apps to take advantage of all the new features.
And every developer we have pretty much is carbonizing their apps right now.
And a carbonized app does get all the new features of Mac OS 10, they just pop to life.
And lastly, Cocoa.
Cocoa is the most advanced object oriented API out there.
It's a wonderful way to write new applications.
You can write them up to 10 times faster than you can with any other technology that is now out there in the mainstream.
So, these are our APIs and across all of them, we have a new user interface called Aqua.
So this is the architecture.
Now there's some new things in the public beta that you may not have seen before unless you're a developer.
The first one is OpenGL.
The second one is a full implementation of Java 2.

We've been working very closely with Sun and not only is our Java 2 implementation really fast, but we've tied it into all of the Aqua user interface elements.
So it's beautiful.
Looks very, very much more beautiful than any Java implementation I think you may have seen.
We support symmetric multiprocessing, so you can take advantage of your dual processor G4s in the most perfect way.

And here's an interesting one.
In PowerBooks, you know, at this point in time, we were not expecting to support portables that well.
And yet even in the beta, the power management is spectacular and here's another thing.
On portables today, when you wake them up, when you wake up a PowerBook, it takes anywhere from 8 to 22 seconds, depending on the state of the networking.
If the networking is turned off, it's 8 seconds.
If it's turned on and not connected to anything, it can be up to 22 seconds to wake up.
For any of these conditions in Mac OS 10, your PowerBook will wake up from sleep in about 1 second.

It's it's actually really startling.
In the time it takes you to open the lid, it's pretty much woken up.
It's it's neat.
Also, the new finder, you can hide the toolbar if you want to.
You can also

Make a mess of the icons any way you'd like.

And in the dock, some people were having trouble keeping track of what was an application and what was a document.

So we've separated them.

We put a line in the middle, and applications are on the left side, documents are on the right side.

You cannot put one in the wrong place.

So very simple to keep track of things now.

And the dock is just fantastic.

In response to some of our professional customers who've said they love the Aqua interface, but they'd like to get rid of the color sometimes for dealing with very important color calibration and documents, we've put in a professional mode, which basically turns all the color in every app to graphite.

We have a new QuickTime player that's fantastic.

It's got the tone controls up here as you can see.

And it does not have the drawer anymore for the QuickTime channels.

You push the button right on the player and the channels just pop up right in the window, so you don't have that drawer popping out.

We've also added an MP3 player and a little audio player that plays CDs.

In Mac OS 10 in the beta, we also have a fantastic version of Internet Explorer that's been carbonized running on 10.

And that joins a few dozen applications like a whole new mail application and all new system administration applications which are shipping with Mac OS 10.

So what I'd love to do now is give you a demo.

This is one of the screen savers that goes and finds all your icons and makes a screen saver.

Okay.

So, Mac OS 10.

Now, for those of you that have not seen Mac OS 10 before, it's a little different in that when you move windows around, the whole window moves around with its contents, not just an outline.

And when you resize a window, it actually does it in real time.

You can see the scroll bars moving, etcetera, right?

Very, very simple.

And it's just unlike anything you've ever experienced on a Mac before.

Very nice.

Let me give you another cool thing about Windows too.

Um, when you have a multitasking system and you get panels, you get alerts or dialogues, right now in the Mac, oftentimes it freezes the Mac.

You cannot do something else until you've dismissed those dialogues as an example.

But even if you could, you would get confused as to which window that dialogue was associated with.

So we've solved this problem in a wonderful way.

Let's say that I want to save this document.

I'll do a save as.

That's the panel.

It's attached to the window.

Just comes right down here.

And this is the save panel.

Now, you might say, well, what if the window's really small?

Well, that's what happens.

You might say, you know, what if the window's over near the edge of the screen?

Well, that happens.

So the level of fit and finish in Mac OS 10 is very, very high.

Now, I want to show you something having to do with the save panel that illustrates the philosophy of Mac OS 10.

We've gone through the OS and we've looked at everything and asked, how can we simplify this?

And how can we make it more powerful at the same time?

So this is an example.

In the save panel here, you notice this is the simplest save panel you've ever seen.

And you just name the document and a pop-up list gives you all your favorite places, right?

To the desktop or wherever, and all the recent places that you've saved documents.

But what if you want to save it to somewhere that's not on one of those lists?

documents.title: Apple Expo Paris 2004
documents.speaker: Steve Jobs
documents.content:
I don't know how I top that.
I should just walk back off stage and say thank you very much and good night.

That's an awesome, awesome welcome.
Thank you.
And uh to everyone watching here and and there'll be a lot of people who get to watch this later on today on the internet, um there could not be a better place to have a show than Paris at the end of summer.
I mean it's a gorgeous day out there in the city.
It's an incredible time and and Apple Expo this year looks to be a huge hit yet again.
We have more vendors than we did last year exhibiting at the show and a big jump up even more in attendance with people pre-registering to be here at the show.
So Apple Expo is going to be amazing and and for all those who watch on the internet who who can't be here, we can only say we wish you were here, but we're really glad we're here.
It's incredible in Paris.
Yes.

Oh, before we begin, I would like to pass on some words from Steve.
As you know, uh Steve loves coming to Paris and wishes he could be here.
And he asked me to pass along that while he can't be here, I think you all know, he's at home recuperating from his successful surgery.
And many of us have had a chance to meet with him and and check up on him and he's doing great.
And he's and he's really, really coming along well and and as you know, he'll be back at work in September.
September can't come soon enough.
Yes.

So I know, I I know I speak for all of us here that we really look forward to Steve coming back to Apple this September.
So let's get started with our show.
I'm going to start by first talking about our music products.
I think you know a few of them.
You've probably heard about the iPod by now.
Yep, the iPod comes in two amazing models now.
The iPod Mini, it's 5 gigabyte hard drive and five really fun colors and the all new fourth generation white iPod.
This new iPod has been a huge hit.
It's a great new design.
It integrates the click wheel from the iPod Mini into the white iPod and it has a lot of great new features like my favorite, the shuffle songs menu right in the top level of the menu.
So with one click, you get access to all your music library randomly.
So as you're running along the beach or biking, you can have access to everything on your on your iPod.
And it's hard to believe, but this new iPod design is even slightly thinner than the previous models.
Yet it still holds its 20 and 40 gigabyte hard drives and 5 to 10,000 songs.
And more importantly, it's increased battery life, 50% more battery life to 12 hours.
So this great new iPod and the successful iPod Mini continues the great success story that is iPod.
For example, the market share of the iPod is measured in the US by NPD has gone up again, 58%.
Now this is the market share of all MP3 players.
That's both flash based and hard drive based.
And so while we know there are a lot of music players in the market, more and more customers choose the iPod.
And we all know why that is, right?
Because it's the best music player in the market.
And Apple's innovation really shows in this great product.
Well we're starting, what we hope is the beginning of yet another great holiday season.
We hope a lot of people find iPods under their Christmas tree.
We're going to start the marketing off with a bang by coming out with yet another version of our great silhouette TV ad.
So what I'd like to do is show you the brand new silhouette TV ad that just started running this weekend, first on MTV.
Let's run that new ad.

Yeah, isn't that cool?

There it is from the side.
Again from the front.
It's a little it's very small.
The slide really looks it's probably about 25 feet big on that slide, but in real life it's smaller than that and it gives incredible dynamic range and base response.
So there's just so many good options for customers now.
The millions and millions of iPod customers can choose from over 250 third party products that work with the iPod and it's a great healthy ecosystem of products growing around the iPod to help us get music around our homes and around our lives.
Well at Apple, we've also been working on some very innovative products to help you get music around your home.
And recently we introduced Airport Express.
And it's starting to get out there and people are realizing what a cool product this is.
Well first of all, it's a base station, just like the Airport base station before it.
And if you want to get wireless internet in your home to get onto broadband via cable or DSL or satellite, this is a great base station to do that.
You just plug it in and now you have wireless access in your house.
Even cooler, it's so small that you can just throw it in your bag and take it with you.
So when you're traveling around the world like many of us do, you plug it in at your hotel room and now you have wireless access in your hotel room as well.
And if you want to extend the airport network in your house, this also works automatically with that.
You can have a base station already in your home, you add a second Airport Express and now you have a wider coverage throughout your home.
So it's a great base station in many ways, but the really cool thing is what it does with music.
It has a stereo jack on the bottom of it.
You plug in your stereo system, analog or digital optical stereo.
And now around your house, you have a wireless network for music.
This is a pretty big breakthrough.
So imagine you have a Mac in your bedroom and you want to stream music to a stereo in your kitchen, just put an Airport Express there and do that.
Or perhaps you have a PC.
Yes, some people do have PCs.
And we need to get music out of them as well, out of iTunes, and you can stream perhaps to your stereo in your living room.
So it really is the first successful wireless network for music in your home.
And it's so easy to use, which is what you'd expect from Apple.
It integrates completely with our great iTunes music software.
When you plug in speakers into your Airport Express, a menu automatically shows up in iTunes that lets you access all those speaker systems you set up.
And you just pull down to where you want the music to go.
You select perhaps your living room, your home theater setup or wherever your speakers are and the music now gets sent there wirelessly from iTunes.
So that integration of software and hardware that Apple is renowned for is just a tremendous simple solution for our customers with Airport Express and iTunes.
So that's the new Airport Express and it's one of the coolest ways to get music around your home and in your life.
Well the other area I mentioned was the car.
We're just at the beginning of a a really big revolution of integrating the iPod with cars and who better to start that with than with BMW.
BMW is a great company that also understands innovative products and we've been working with them on the first true seamless integration of the iPod and an automobile.
So for example, today what you would have to do in your car to get music through your your car stereo and a lot of us all do this is we for example buy a cassette adapter and you plug it into the headphone jack of your iPod.
Then you get an AC adapter that plugs into your cigarette lighter and plug that in to keep charging your iPod and now you have music wherever you go.
It's not the ideal driving experience, but it's music at least in your car.
Well, what we really want is for it to look like this.
And that's what you can do with the iPod adapter from BMW.
You can use the iPod in your car and yet have the gorgeous environment you want.
So where is the iPod?
Well, it's in the glove box.
There's a single cable there that plugs right into the connector on the bottom of the iPod and over that connector you get great quality stereo audio, you get power charging your iPod.
It's even smart enough to deactivate the buttons on the iPod so nothing in your glove box accidentally bumps it and changes your music when you don't want it to.
Just close up your glove box and you get driving.
So maybe you're racing down the Autobahn at 200 kilometers per hour, blowing somebody by and you want to crank up the tunes, you can do it right on your steering wheel.
Sounds like fun to me.
Of course, you can also control it from the stereo head unit in your car.
It uses the same interface as you're used to with a CD player, but instead of controlling CDs, you're now controlling your playlist up to six playlists on your iPod and those songs on that playlist.
That's just a little bit about the things we're doing to not only make great iPods, but to make digital music part of our life all around our house.
So you can get access to your music wherever you are and in your car while you're driving.
Now BMW is actually here at Apple Expo.
They have cars at the show so you can check it out.
And they'll be talking about how you can now be able to get uh support in your BMW in Europe this fall with BMW authorized service centers.
So it's starting to come to Europe as well.
Let's talk about the music store.
Along with having a great jukebox and a great iPod, what's really brought this all together and made sense for all of us is the ability to finally legally buy music on the internet through the iTunes Music Store, the first successful music store.
Well, as you know, we started this in the US.
In the US, we've built a library of over a million songs that customers can purchase and download.
And recently this summer, we we announced that we've passed the 100 million song mark for songs sold.
Something never done before, a major milestone.
Yes.

So certainly congratulations goes to the iTunes team, iTunes Music Store team.
You don't know how hard they work day and night getting great music and great services to everybody.
This doesn't come easy and they work so hard to be as successful as they are.
And and it shows in our market share.
We're not the only music store that customers can buy music from, but we're the best music store and that's why so many people choose to buy music on iTunes because we work hardest and deliver the best music experience.
Well, based on customer demand, of course, we had to bring it to Europe.
Customers over here really asked us to bring the iTunes Music Store and we started this year.
We started first in the UK, France and Germany.
And as you know, we've built a library in Europe over over 700,000 songs and we're investing a lot in that and growing it every day.
We have a lot of great music from the five majors as well as increasingly from dozens and dozens of independent music companies.
Great bands like with exclusive content like Bon, Rune 5 and and Schiller.
Yeah.
Yeah, great band.
Well, I'm sure I'm sure you've heard some of the results of that.
In the first week, we sold over 800,000 songs in those three countries.
And that was a big accomplishment.
That was 16 times the closest competitor.
As I said, there were already music stores in Europe, none as great as the iTunes Music Store.
So how have we done since then?
You might be wondering.
It's been 10 weeks since we introduced that music store in the UK, France and Germany.
And in that time, I'm happy to announce we've sold 5 million songs.

So what are our plans with the music store in Europe?
Well, to bring it to more and more of our European customers as more and more people want access to this great technology.
We started in the US, we brought it to the UK, France and Germany and our next stop is to bring it in October across the EU countries with an English store accessible by more and more countries.
So we're going to continue to bring the iTunes Music Store across Europe and allow it to grow by just meeting the needs of all the customers who want it so badly.
So that's an update on our music products on the iPod and the iTunes Music Store and what a great success they are.
We continue to work hard and innovate in the space like no one else.
I now talk about the Mac.
MacOS 10, the current release Panther has been the best release we've ever had of MacOS, both in units sold as well as the number of customers now using MacOS 10.
And really the transition is over.
The majority of our customers all use MacOS 10.
The majority of our developers are now delivering only MacOS 10 software and there are great software applications available.
Over 12,000 native applications and growing every day on MacOS 10.
And as you go through the show here in Paris at Apple Expo, you're going to see more and more new products that are available and being announced here at the show.
Just to name a few of them, Quark is delivering Quark Express.

Hold on, my button's having some fun.
We don't make these clickers.
We're having fun with slides.
There we go.
Quark Express is showing off Quark's QPS system running on Xserves.
Uh 4D, that great database created over here in Europe has the new 2004 version.
Alias is showing their new high-end Maya Unlimited running on MacOS 10.
Lego has worked with Feral Interactive to deliver a brand new Bionicle game on the Mac as well as other gaming platforms.
Vara is bringing the new Video Q software, which is great multimedia presentation software on MacOS 10.
And Hachette Multimedia is a French encyclopedia and those are just a few examples of all the great software that you're going to find here at Apple Expo and the tremendous momentum on MacOS 10 from our developers.
I'd like to show you two products specifically because they're so much fun and give you a sense of the great things happening on MacOS 10.
First, THQ, they're a game developer working with a really major fun movie studio who's launching a new movie and they have a killer game coming out on the Mac tying in with that movie.
I'd like to introduce Shiraz Akmal.
He's the director of development for THQ.
Shiraz?

shared between Mac and Windows clients. And to be able to create richer emails using standard HTML composition for sharing with Windows customers. And a lot of little attention to detail like you may not realize it that the the built-in word processor in Mac OS 10 text edit has the ability already to open word files. Well, now with Tiger, we've added support for word files that have tables included in them. So many touches to make the integration in the Windows world easier for Mac OS 10 customer.

But Mac OS 10 isn't just about fitting in. It's about standing out with innovative new features. And both we and Microsoft are talking about the next great thing in an operating system, and that's search. Search is the next big revolution in personal computer operating systems. And again, we know where we're going in Mac OS 10 and Tiger. We have a clear vision. Um, it seems like there's some turmoil on the other side of where they're going. And so again, no need to to tease them here for their for their problems. Uh, they they can't figure it out, but what we have is an amazing solution.

And so why do we care? Well, it used to be really easy. You would create a folder, you put a file in it, and you know where it is. But more and more with these 20 and 30 and 40 gigabyte systems with thousands and thousands of files, it's becoming harder and harder to find our documents on our system. A lot of people joke or complain that it's actually easier to go into Google and search the internet for a site out of a billion sites and find it in a second than it is to find something in your own hard drive. Right? Well, we've got to solve that. That's not okay.

So we've been hard at work at the technology to solve that problem. The easier thing was figuring out how to create an underlying system that can find something really fast. The hard thing was to figure out how to make that easy to use. And as we thought about it and worked on it, it became apparent to us that we already had an answer. We solved this in iTunes. In iTunes, we created a system where you can have thousands and thousands of songs, but you just start to type in a few letters of what you want and instantly you find it. And it doesn't matter what you're typing in, an artist name, a song title, the name of an album, a genre. You just start typing and iTunes finds what you want in a split second. The more you type, the more refined your search. That's how search should work in a personal computer.

So that's what we set out to do, to build that kind of technology in at the system level and help your entire personal computer experience. So search is the next major feature of Tiger, the most important breakthrough feature. And we call it Spotlight. And Spotlight is going to make a lot of things we need to do every day really easy. Like, for example, coming over here, I probably need to get a hold of all the documents that are being created for coming to the Apple Expo. It doesn't matter what kind of application they were used or where they come from, what directories they're in. I just need to find them all and manage them. Or maybe something detailed, like I want to keep track of all the 1200 DPI CMYK images that Ken sent to me. I should be able to do that on my computer.

Or something as broad as I just want to track everything on my computer about Bertrand. I want to know his contact information, email messages we've exchanged, meetings we have coming up. I want that all to work together. Well, Spotlight does that, and it does it in a way that's just super fast, just like iTunes. And it's automatic. It works with standard file formats, like MPEGs and JPEGs and MPEG movies and MP3 music files and all the things that you're used to just work within Spotlight. And developers who create new file formats can extend it and make sure they work with Spotlight. It works with your current applications and documents. You don't have to upgrade your apps, you don't have to change your documents. They'll now work with Spotlight.

And it finds both content, the things you have in your document like words you type in a letter, as well as the metadata or information about the document, like who sent it to you or when did you last look at it. So we're building Spotlight into the system. We're building it into work in the Finder, as well as many of the system applications we all use. We're building Spotlight to work with your address book and your preferences and mail and iChat and iCal, make it all work together and make our personal computer experience much better. So let me go over to a system here and give you a demo of Spotlight right now.

So here I am in Mac OS 10 in Tiger. Now, this is the first time we've shown this publicly. So we'll keep our fingers crossed that the demo gods are with us and that everything works as as promised. Thanks for coming this morning. And um, we've got some fun stuff to uh share with you this morning. Uh, and uh because we're in a more intimate setting, I thought it'd be be kind of nice to let some of the folks that worked on these projects, some of the engineers, uh demo them to you. So uh we're going to have a few colleagues up here showing you stuff. I'm going to be a little like a yo-yo. Uh but that's fine. And so I'd like to start um with the state of the Mac. We're going to be talking about the Mac today. And to uh to take us through the state of the Mac, I'd like to invite my colleague Tim Cook, our chief operating officer up to take us through that.

Thanks, Tim. You know, I could hear a lot of phones beeping. So could we just take a minute, maybe everybody could flip the silencer on their phones? Thank you. Um, so that's the state of the Mac. Now let's move on to some new products. I'd like to talk about iLife. iLife is widely regarded as the best suite of sort of digital life applications in the world. And it's why some people buy a Mac because you can do amazing things with your photos, your videos, and music that you can't do on any other personal computer or with any other software. And we keep improving it every year or two, coming out with a new version and it's gotten incredibly good. Well, we've got a new version we're announcing today, which is iLife 11. It's got the same apps in it and we'd like to give you a little uh look at three of them today. So the first one is iPhoto. It's the most popular app of the suite. And iPhoto 11's got some great features. You know, we tried in the last release this new thing which was a full-screen mode. So you could go into full-screen mode and do a few things in iPhoto. And the response has been so great that we're really fleshing out the full-screen mode so you can just live full-screen in iPhoto and it's wonderful. We've got a lot of Facebook enhancements where you can even more easily post to Facebook and even see people's responses back uh to the photos that you've posted. We've made it really easy and elegant to email photos to people from iPhoto without ever leaving iPhoto. We've added some beautiful new slideshows. A big leap in books. You know, we we're printing now over 2 million books a year. And um we've got a big leap now in how you make those books and the quality of the printing and it's really nice. And we're adding beautiful letterpress cards as well. So a lot of great stuff uh in iPhoto 11 and to take us through a demo of that, I'd like to ask Phil Schiller, our vice president, senior vice president of worldwide product marketing.

I think that's awesome.

This is why we do what we do.

So, we've taken iPhoto and broadened out the full screen mode so you can live in full screen. Really taken the books up a big notch, allowing you to create just the most beautiful books and these letter press cards, unlike anything we've seen a computer do before. And all your projects together in one place. So we're really excited about these new features and that is iPhoto 11. Next up, iMovie. This is a great release. iMovie 11. Now, the number one request we got after the last version of iMovie was for better audio editing. And the team has gone above and beyond the call of duty and come up with something great. What we strive for in iMovie is to be able to do extremely sophisticated editing really simply, so that all of us mere mortals who don't want to learn how to use Final Cut Pro say, uh, can make these amazing movies. And that's what the team has done. All new audio editing, something called one step effects, which you'll see, which are remarkable, a people finder to help you find clips with people in them. News and sports themes and something we're really excited about, the ability to construct movie trailers with almost no effort. This is going to be really fun. People are going to use this a lot. And so to show you iMovie 11, I'd like to invite Randy Ubillos, who's our chief architect for video applications, up to show you iMovie 11. Randy.

Awesome.

That awesome. You know, Randy, along with his team have invented all of this stuff. It's amazing. So, iMovie 11, and we think it's a real breakthrough and we think people are going to have tons of fun rapidly being able to create stuff like this, posting it on Facebook, posting it on YouTube, posting it on Vimeo. It's going to be great. So a lot of great new features in iMovie 11. We also have a new GarageBand. GarageBand 11. GarageBand 11's got some great features to help you fix the timing of the rhythm in your music, something called Flex Time, something called Groove Matching, as well as a bunch of other stuff including more guitar amps and uh effects and new piano uh and guitar lessons including a fictu a feature called how did I play? And we think this stuff's going to be really well received and to show it to us is Xander Soren, product marketing manager.

And this is great. But as we've added full screen apps now, we say, you know, we have four of these things. Wouldn't it be great to unify them all? And so we've done that in something we call Mission Control. It's a way to view everything running on your Mac and instantly navigate to anywhere. So what we'd like to do now is even though we have tons of new features in line, we've picked out a few of them and we'd like to give you a sneak peek today. And to do that, I'd like to ask Craig Federighi, who's our Vice President of Engineering for Mac OS 10, to come give us a demo.

Thanks, Craig.

Thank you, Craig. We're really excited about Lion. We think bringing some of these things back to the Mac and coming up with some very fresh new things, uh, like Mission Control, is going to really delight Mac users. So again, a whole new way of getting apps with the App Store, of finding and launching apps with Launchpad, being able to work in full screen and move between full screen apps effortlessly, and then moving back to your windows and, of course, Mission Control. And again, I wish we had another hour and a half to show you more, uh, but, uh, we'll unveil this over time as we get closer to releasing it. Our plan is to release Lion this summer, summer 2011. And, uh, we are on schedule for that. We're feeling real good about it. So that is Mac OS 10 Lion. Now, I want to go back and talk for a minute about the App Store. Um, the Mac App Store is is, uh, we think going to be really great for our users, and we don't want to wait for Lion. So we've decided that we're going to put out the Mac App Store on Snow Leopard, and we're going to open it within 90 days. The Mac App Store is going to open within 90 days from today, and you developers can go to our website and learn all about it today, and we are going to be accepting app submissions from developers in November. That's next month for the store that's going to open within 90 days. So we're very excited about that. And that is Lion, the App Store opening with 90 days. And again, back to the Mac, let me review some of the things we talked about today. Tim took us through the state of the Mac. The Mac is a third of our revenue. We pay a lot of attention to it. We love the Mac. We're investing heavily in the Mac. It's a $22 billion business, which if it was a standalone business, would be a rather large business in the Fortune 500. Our retail market share has topped 20% for the first time in a long while. And we continue to invest in our retail stores. We couldn't be happier with the performance of them and how they're bringing more and more people into the Mac tent. iLife 11, phenomenal new applications. iPhoto 11, full screen mode, better books, all new letter press cards. iMovie 11, you can imagine how we're all going to use this. And GarageBand, giving those millions and millions of GarageBand users even cooler things they can do now with their compositions and in learning how to play instruments. FaceTime on Mac, so that the tens of millions of Mac users can now FaceTime with our mobile devices. We think this is going to be very popular. And Lion, coming this summer with amazing features like Mission Control, the Launchpad, and the App Store. And with the App Store opening within 90 days from today. So this is these are the things that we wanted to share with you today. We're really excited about them. But there is one more thing. And, uh, that one more thing really comes back to our theme for today, which is back to the Mac. You know, we talked about this virtuous circle with Mac OS 10 helping to create iOS for our devices, that maturing, being on the iPod as well, and now being inspired by that, bringing some of that back to Mac OS 10. But just like that philosophy has some benefit in our software, it can also have some benefit in our hardware. What would happen if a MacBook met an iPad? There's a lot to be inspired about there as well. Well, what are some of those things? An iPad has instant on, right? That's pretty rare for a notebook. Great battery life, amazing standby time, 30-day standby time, solid state storage, so there's no optical or hard drives. And it's thinner and lighter, which means it's even more mobile. These are some great things for notebooks. And so we asked ourselves, what would happen if a MacBook and an iPad hooked up?

Well, this is the result. It's one of the most amazing things we've ever created. It is our new MacBook Air, and we think it's the future of notebooks. We're really excited about this. It is gorgeous. Let me just show you a few beautiful shots of it. It's like nothing we've ever created before, and it's it's really stunning. And it's really small. It's amazingly thin. At its thickest point, it is 0.68 inches thin at its thickest point. And it tapers down to just 0.11 inches at its thinnest point. That's a tenth of an inch. And it weighs just 2.9 pounds. Now, it's really it's hard enough to build something thin, but we also want our products to be rigid and durable. And so the new MacBook Air is complete unibody construction. Complete aluminum unibody construction. It's pretty amazing. It's got a full-size keyboard and a full-size glass trackpad. These are areas where you do not want to sacrifice. So let me tell you a bit about it. The first thing is, it's got a 13.3 inch LED backlit display, and it's a high-res display, 1440 by 900 pixels. This is more pixels than are on our 15-inch notebook today. More pixels than on the 15-inch MacBook Pro. It's got a Core 2 Duo processor, which is a fast processor for this class of machine, and great graphics, great Nvidia GeForce graphics. Full-size keyboard, full-size multi-touch trackpad, and a FaceTime camera. Now, just as interesting as what it's got is what it doesn't have. There is no optical drive, and there is no hard drive. We have gone to flash storage, complete solid state storage. Now, why do we do this? Because we know the benefits from the iPad. Instant on. It's up to two times faster than hard drives. That's a lot. It's much more reliable, especially in a mobile environment, and it's 90% smaller and lighter. Again, very important in the mobile environment. It also gives you completely silent operation. Now, we know a lot about flash. We've designed it into our iPhones, we've designed it into our iPads. And as you may know, Apple is the largest user of flash memory in the world. So we know a lot about creating flash storage subsystems. Battery life on the new MacBook Air, wireless web tests, 7 hours, standby, 30 days. 30-day standby time instead of the few days we get with today's notebooks. Now, the wireless web tests as well, you know, we've the PC industry's battery tests sometimes don't reflect real world results. And, uh, we're moving towards some more stringent tests that really we think are going to get us much closer to real world results on battery tests. And even using these more stringent tests, we're getting 7 hours of wireless web battery life. Our previous MacBook Air using the old, more liberal tests got only five. So we're really happy with this improvement in battery life. We think it's a double improvement, not only from five to seven, but with we think much more realistic testing. So, what's inside this puppy? Well, let's take a look. We have flash storage. Again, we don't put it inside a big SSD container. We put flash basically right on the board. That's how we do it in the iPad, the iPods, the iPhone. 80211n Wi-Fi wireless networking. There is our Core 2 Duo processor and our graphics processor. Our memory, stereo speakers, and our battery. You can see what the biggest thing in this is. It's the battery. If we take out the battery, you can see how small the electronics are. That's an entire high-performance Mac on that tiny little board. We've taken everything we've learned about miniaturization from from iPods, iPhones, and iPads and applied it to the Mac. We're really, really excited about this. Now, this 13.3 inch MacBook Air isn't the whole story, because it has a younger brother, too. In addition to the 13.3 inch, its younger brother is an 11.6 inch, even smaller, even lighter, 2.3 pounds. And it's also an amazing product. It's got all the things that the 13-inch has, processor and video graphics, full-size keyboard even on the smaller unit, multi-touch trackpad, FaceTime camera, and, of course, it has an 11.6 inch LED backlit display and also high resolution. This is more dots than our 13-inch MacBook Pro has.

has today.

So, a high resolution, wide screen 11.6 inch display.

And it gets a battery life of five hours on the wireless web, again using those same more rigorous tests, and the same 30 uh 30 days of standby time.

We've tried to be really aggressive.

So these are great from an environmental and toxics point of view.

So we're really excited about these new MacBook Airs.

And I'm really pleased to say that both of them are available starting today.

So, we made an ad.

And if you'd like, I'd love to show you the ad.

Why don't we roll it?

Feel simple?

And we've also made a nice video that I'd love to show you, kind of summarizes everything we've talked about about the MacBook Air.

Let's go ahead and run that too.

So, we're really proud of this.

We want you to get your hands on it.

So we've got a hands-on room set up right across the way here for all of you to be able to go touch one of these and use one of these yourself and I I think you're going to be pretty amazed.

We certainly are.

And uh we hope our customers are.

**[Narrator]**: I mean our our learning just keeps building from one project to the next to the next.

**[Narrator]**: That's absolutely the case here.

**[Narrator]**: I mean years and years of designing such a range of different products enables the design of the new MacBook Air.

**[Steve Jobs]**: So, we're really proud of this.

**[Steve Jobs]**: We want you to get your hands on it.

**[Steve Jobs]**: And uh we hope our customers are.

**[Steve Jobs]**: We really appreciate your coming and we'll see you over in the hands-on room as we get back to the Mac.

**[Steve Jobs]**: Thanks very much.

3D rendering for the dock. But I don't know about, um, you, but my desktop sometimes has a little more clutter. And we've had a feature for the longest time on how to deal with clutter. It's called Expose. So what we did is we've built Expose into the dock. The way it works is you just click and hold on an app tile. Et voila, you select the window you want.

Next installation. That's probably your first contact with Snow Leopard. And we've made it even faster, up to 45% faster.

But maybe more importantly, after you install Snow Leopard, you actually recover some disk space.

Over Over half the footprint of the OS, over 6 gigabyte more space, thanks to technologies like file system compression. Preview. Preview is of course our favorite way to view images and PDF files, and we've made common operations faster. There's also lots of little touches. One I like is about text selection in PDF files. In Leopard, you can actually select text and copy paste it into other applications, but it doesn't always follow the logical order of the text. In Snow Leopard, we've used a little bit of AI to actually infer the structure of the document.

Next, Chinese input methods. It can be cumbersome to enter a character, a Chinese character with a keyboard. But you've got a trackpad. Why not use it? This is exactly what we did with Snow Leopard. You can draw with your finger. And the computer picks the most appropriate character, even predicts the next character to come. Next, mail. Everyone uses mail. We've made it even faster, and quite a bit faster for common operations, as you can see.

Next, Safari. We've been working on a new version of Safari called Safari 4 with features like top sites. It's been in beta for a couple of months and I'm very proud to announce that today we are shipping Safari 4 for Leopard, Tiger, and Windows.

Safari 4 offers unsurpassed speed. Speed for HTML and speed for JavaScript for your web 2.0 web pages. This chart here shows the standard Sun Spider JavaScript benchmark and the scale is multiples of IE8 speed.

It's also very, very standard. In fact, the gold standard for the the ultimate test for standardness is the acid 3 test and it passes 100%. To put that in perspective, IE8 passes 21%. So, Safari 4, of course, will also be available on Snow Leopard. It will be included in Snow Leopard. And in Snow Leopard, there's a couple extra features you don't get on the other platforms. The first is crash resistance. Let's say you browse the web, have quite a bit of state build up. Well, let me tell you a little secret. The number one cause of crashes across all of Mac OS 10 is actually browser plugins. So if your plugin crashes in Snow Leopard, you just get this rectangle, but the rest of your windows are intact.

All you need to do is reload that page and that's it. You haven't missed a beat in your browsing. The second feature that you get only on Snow Leopard is even more speed. You know the JavaScript benchmark I showed you a few slides ago? That's a 32-bit benchmark. When you run in 64-bit, you go even faster. And of course, we run the application in 64-bit. QuickTime. We have an all new QuickTime in Snow Leopard. We call it QuickTime 10. It's an all modern stack. It fully leverages hardware acceleration. It's super efficient. It's color correct and we're debuting a new technology for streaming called HTTP streaming because it's all based on standards, HTTP, AAC, H264. It works with any web server, like an Apache server. It's really cool. So since we had such a change in the back end of QuickTime, we decided to also change the user interface of the QuickTime player. And this is what it looks like. As you can see, the content is center stage. In fact, as you start playing, the on-screen controls, including the window title, go away to let you enjoy your contents. So what I'd like to do now is have you see some of the features and little touches that we've added in Snow Leopard. And for that, I'd like to ask my colleague Craig Federighi, VP of Mac OS Engineering, to demo to us some of the refinements.

Thanks Craig.

So lots of refinements in Snow Leopard. But there's also powerful new technologies. And those technologies fundamentally are to take advantage of the power of silicon and bring that to the user experience. Because when you look at a modern Macintosh, you have an incredible set of components, things that weren't thinkable a few years ago. You have RAM, gigabytes of RAM. I mean, a few years ago it was expressed in megabytes. You have a powerful processor that runs at a frequency expressed in gigahertz that's multicore, 64-bit capable. And then you have a GPU with enormous raw processing power. But to take advantage of all this, you need the right software. So we have a number of technologies. I want to mention three. First, 64-bit. Of course, the primary reason to use 64-bit is to take advantage of lots of memory because if your application runs in 32-bit mode, it has an inherent limit with the addressing space at 4 gigabytes. When you run in 64-bit, it's 16 billion gigabytes. That's the limit of your addressing space. In practice, it's unlimited. Another reason of course to run 64-bit is that the processor can do math faster. So certain things like FFTs will run twice as fast in 64-bit mode. So for all those reasons, we've been on a trajectory over the last few releases to enable more and more 64-bit and Snow Leopard is the final stage where we are running all the major system applications in 64-bit mode. So,

That's 64-bit. Now let's talk about multicore because Moore's law has changed its form. You know, a few years ago we were used to always increasing kind of frequency for the chips. And as the processors hit around 3 gigahertz or something like that, the expression of Moore's law became there's more and more cores. And this is a trend that we see continuing in the future. But the challenge with multicore is how to take advantage of them, how to program them. And the standard answer is threads, multithreaded programming, but it's really, really hard and it's also fairly inefficient because you never have quite the right granularity. So we have a solution for this, a new methodology that we called Grand Central Dispatch. It's built in support for multicore across all of Snow Leopard. It's very, very comprehensive. All the way from a language extension, low-level libraries that are super efficient, high-level libraries to make it really easy to program, integration with all the system APIs and tools to tune your program. So just to give you a test of what it feels to use GCD, let's look at threads in Leopard for say the mail application. When mail is busy, it has a certain number of threads and when it's idle, it actually keeps pretty much all those threads. In Snow Leopard, when mail is busy, it actually uses more threads to take advantage of the multicore. But when mail is idle in Snow Leopard, all those threads go away, giving back resources to the system. And when you reapply that pattern for every major application, you get a big win in performance and responsiveness. So that's GCD for multicore. Next, let's talk graphics. You know, the amount of power that you have in cards nowadays is incredible. We are talking of over one teraflop in raw power. That's 1 trillion operations per second. It would have taken a whole room a few years ago to have that kind of raw power. And the standard way to use that power is to use OpenGL. That's what's used for games and graphics. But we want to move beyond that. We want to use this power for all kinds of things. And for that, we've devised a technology that we call OpenCL. The C stands for computing. It protects you as developers from exactly what card the user has. It's based on C, so there's very low learning curve. It uses sophisticated compilation techniques to optimize and it has numerical accuracy, which means you can use that for scientific computation. We've also decided to make it an open standard and many companies are participating.

In fact, all the top manufacturers of graphics chip are in. So that's OpenCL. So just three of the technologies we have in Snow Leopard, they are really important because they give us a lot of power in the platform. And this power is power for us to innovate in the OS and it's power for you, for your applications to gain a competitive edge. So the next area I wanted to cover is fitting in businesses. You know, many people nowadays have a Mac at home that they want to take to work and it works great because we have Microsoft Office. That's of course the de facto standard. We integrate really well with IT services. We have Unix.

And we can run Windows applications via Boot Camp, Parallels, or VMware.

internet connection with your computer.
