documents.title: WWDC 1999
documents.speaker: Steve Jobs
documents.content:
Good morning.

Good morning, all the way back there. We have some great stuff today, and uh it's my pleasure to get us going here this morning. So welcome to our 1999 Worldwide Developers Conference. This year is a record year for Apple. We've got over 2500 people here as paid attendees. That's over a 40% increase from last year. And based on what's happened this last year, it's clear that developers are back on the Mac, and it's really great. We've got people from 48 states. We've got people here from 38 countries, and we have over 200 student developers here, which I think is incredibly great.

Now, I just want to take us back a year. It was a year ago last week that we announced the iMac. I know for some of us it seems longer than that, but it really was only a year. And in the last year, we all know what's happened. But one of the things that's happened is that a lot of Macintosh apps were announced since a year ago last week. How many? You probably haven't been counting, but but we have. And it's also a record number. Over 3100 Mac apps have been announced.

And this this is phenomenal, and our message today, and the key message I want to start off with is thank you guys. You guys have been awesome. And you've hung in there, and you've given us the time to turn this thing around and get the volumes back up, and we really, really deeply appreciate it. So thank you very much.

Now, we're not going to announce a lot of new applications coming out here today because we just don't have the time to cover everything, but there's one in particular that uh I would like to highlight today. It's an application area that we think is very important today. We think it's very important for the future, and we're extraordinarily excited uh to announce today that Dragon Systems is going to be bringing their incredible speech recognition technology to the Macintosh. And today with us, we have Janet Baker, their co-founder and CEO.

Thank you.

We're really excited about this, and I think it's something a lot of our applications and our system software can take true advantage of. Now, I'd like to run through and give you an update on Apple really quick, and then we'll get into the heart of the matter, which is of course the updates on all of our software and where we're going. So first, the company. Now, when we last met a year ago, we had just finished our second quarter of profitability. And I know a lot of you were asking the question, well, you know, can this continue? And I'm very pleased to report a year later that it did continue. And Apple has seen some some healthy profits in the last year since we've met. And we've also seen some healthy unit growth. This has been fantastic. We've gone from sort of the mid-600s to the mid-800s, even climbing up to the mid-900s during that Christmas quarter uh just a few months ago. So we're very pleased with the unit volume, and we think it will continue to stay healthy. In terms of inventory, I just want to highlight this. I know this isn't something that maybe most of you care too much about, but we care deeply about it because our inventory costs more than yours. And we have to manage it really well because this stuff gets obsolete just sitting on the shelf. And we have done, I think a terrific job in doing that over the last several quarters. And as you see, in the last three quarters, we've gotten down, so these are days of inventory leaving each quarter. So we used to have 30, and we literally last left left last quarter with one day of inventory. And during the last three quarters, we have beat Dell. And Apple has become Apple has become in many ways the most operationally excellent company now in this industry. And we think that's very important. And lastly again, cash. I think when we look back a year ago, there were still some questions about Apple's financial stability. Those questions have, I hope, evaporated by now. Apple is in very strong shape financially. So, that's just a brief update on the company, and now uh what we'd really like to do is is get into software. But as a last comment on the company state, I don't think there's ever been a better time to be a Mac developer.

Next, I'd just like to cover the products a little bit. Where are we with the products? As you know, this is our product strategy. We have a very, very simple product strategy. Two pro products, those are the ones on the right, the Power Mac and the PowerBook. And soon to be two consumer products, iMac and a consumer portable, which we will announce a little later this year. So let's take a look at each of these. Let's first take a look at the iMacs. You're familiar with, whoops, you're familiar with Lifesavers. Uh we that was our internal code name for the colored iMacs. We introduced them in January, and they have been a huge hit. Our iMac volume is just very, very healthy right now. We're running some fun ads right now. The thrill of surfing, the agony of choosing a color. And we have another one that's kind of fun. It just says, whoops. Surf's up, right? And uh so you'll see this and running a lot of television as well right now. So who's buying all these iMacs? This is this is of paramount concern to or importance to us and to you. So who's buying this? We do a lot of market research. We do it every single quarter, and this is what the latest stuff has said. This data is about uh a month old. Of all the iMacs purchased in the US, 32% are first-time computer buyers. 32%. This is way above the industry average. And 13% Wintel converts. So 45% of iMacs are new iMac customers are new to the Mac platform. 55% are not, but even those 55%, over half of them are replacing their Macs, and that's the time they buy new software. So that's good for all of us. In Japan, the numbers are even more staggering. First-time computer buyers in Japan are 49% of the total. Almost half. So we're like we're really happy about this. And and uh and we want to get even more of those first-time computer buyers. Now, we also in our market research ask some questions. So one of the first questions we ask is, are you connected to the internet? Now the industry average is is is is is fairly low, as you know. On iMac, 89%. That's up from 82% a quarter before. 89% are connected to the internet. When did you get connected? As you know, iMac, you can take it out of the box and in 10 minutes you're surfing the web, right? When did you get connected? 75% of these folks got connected the first day. Next, is iMac your primary internet access device? We want to make sure that people aren't buying an iMac and they get it connected, but then they're using some other computer as their primary internet computer. And that's that's very clear because 87% of them say iMac is their primary internet access device. And is this the first time your home has had internet access? These iMac customers, 79% of them say yes. So if you add all this up, what it says is we're getting a ton of first-time computer buyers who have never been on the internet before, who are taking their iMac home, getting internet access, and getting on the internet. 80% of them. Now, we ask this question a lot. How do we get more customers like these? And there's many answers, and we're doing lots of things. But one is very important, which is we want to continue to carefully and very selectively expand our distribution. And we've looked at a lot of partners, and today we're very happy to announce that we are adding Sears to our stable of national and regional distribution for iMac. And Sears is going to distribute iMac through their 800-some-odd stores that sell computers in the US. They reach 32 million households. Uh 54% of their are computer buyers are first-time buyers, which is exactly the core audience we're going for. And we're going to launch this late this month over the Memorial Day weekend. So we're very, very excited about this, and we think Sears is going to provide a really great buying experience for these iMacs. So that's our iMac update. Next to the Power Mac G3s. I don't have too much new on that except to tell you that our volumes now on this product line are higher than they have been since I returned to the company. We are thrilled at the number of Power Mac G3s we are shipping. And uh I know some of you are customers. Thank you very much. We don't have any new to announce in this product line, but it's doing extremely well since its launch in January. We'll spend some time on PowerBooks today because it's my pleasure today. I know there's been a lot of rumors, and they're true. Uh it's my pleasure to announce the new PowerBook line today. We've got some great products. So when you look when we look at PowerBooks, we say, what do people want? Well, they want these gorgeous 14.1-inch displays. Of course, the new PowerBooks have those. They want DVD drives. The existing PowerBooks with DVD drives have become the best way to watch movies on airplanes, as you know. Uh people want desktop speed. While Wintel world is promising that with some new technology they're going to have late this year, we've been delivering that for over a year. And we have awesome desktop speed. Battery life is key, uh especially if you're watching your movie on that transatlantic flight and you don't even have enough battery to watch the whole movie. And weight, of course. So what are we doing? Our new PowerBooks, two models, 33 333 and 400 MHz. These are the fastest portables in the marketplace. They are running at our desktop speeds. Let's take a look at that. In terms of byte marks, these are the fastest Wintel portables money can buy, right? They're running it up to 366 MHz. And they give you up to about five byte marks. These are our current or actually these are our current and soon to be old PowerBooks. Uh and they get you at 300 MHz running up to 10 byte marks. And these are the two new models taking us over 13 byte marks. As you can see, that's two to three times faster than the fastest Wintel notebooks money can buy. True desktop performance. Take a look at the weight. On the weight, industry standard for a fully featured notebook, you know, with a CD or DVD in it drive, is 7 to 8 pounds. And our current PowerBooks are right in that range. Compact IBM ThinkPads and the Toshibas are the three top-selling Wintel notebooks. That's why I picked them, and that's where they are. The new PowerBook is substantially lighter, 5.9 pounds. It is it is now the lightest notebook in this class. These all have 14-inch screens on them. This is the lightest in its class. Battery life. Battery life is really important, as you know if you use a portable. And again, these are the advertised battery lives of the Compact, the ThinkPad, and the Toshiba. And to be honest, you know, your mileage may vary on these things. You don't usually get this kind of battery life. These are the advertised figures. Current PowerBook is right in there, 3 and 1/2 hours. The new PowerBook on real battery life, real tests. We have a lot of tests that we run on these things, is setting a new industry milestone. 5-hour battery life. And and that's with one battery. You can have two batteries and get 10-hour battery life. **[Speaker 2]**: Yes, we're going to stop making substantial changes like changing the underlying kernel.
At least for this year.

**[Speaker 3]**: So we're really excited about this.
Please get your copy.
Please give us feedback.
And this is what we're doing at Apple.
I'm told this is the third year in a row that we have the same Senior Vice President of Software, Avi Tevanian.

**[Speaker 3]**: I'm actually told that's a record.

**[Speaker 2]**: Yeah, I think that's a record for Apple.

**[Speaker 3]**: And, uh, and, uh, we'll be setting more records there as well.
And in addition to that, um, I'm hoping that our software strategies are starting to sound a little boring to you because they're not changing every year.

**[Audience]**: [Laughter]

**[Speaker 3]**: They're not changing every year.

**[Speaker 2]**: Let's actually review the changes from last year.

**[Speaker 3]**: The changes from last year in our software strategy, I think they're zero.

**[Speaker 2]**: Right.

**[Speaker 3]**: Zero changes.
And so hopefully we're making up from not having the drama of the strategy a year with exciting and timely implementation that is surprising you on the upside, both in how rapidly we're bringing things to market and how good they are when they come out.
And that is our strategy.
So when we meet again next year, we will have accomplished quite a lot, and we will have launched Mac OS 10.
And it's going to be a very exciting year, and if we can get the kind of help that we've gotten from all of you this past year, I know that we will be successful together.
So thank you very much, guys.
Thanks.

documents.title: WWDC 2000
documents.speaker: Steve Jobs
documents.content:
Thank you.

Thank you very much for coming this morning.

We've got a lot of stuff to tell you. Uh, in addition to everybody here and the overflow rooms, uh, I'd like to also mention that we're webcasting this, uh, with ourselves, with QuickTime Live, uh, and using our partner Akamai. We now have over 14,000 live streams and climbing. We're broadcasting these streams up to a gigabit per second. So we're broadcasting now 4 gigabits per second live, uh, out of the Akamai network, uh, using QuickTime. So we've got people all over the country watching this as well.

So let's get started.

I'd first like to start with something that every, almost every Mac user touches.

And that's the mouse.

This, as you may know, is our mouse. And, uh, some people don't like it.

And we, we have many faults, but we do listen. And, uh, so, you know, some people think that this is the worst mouse in the world. We'd like to change that. And today, we are introducing a new mouse.

Now, this mouse, we may go from what some people think is the worst mouse in the industry to the best.

The first thing about this mouse that's extraordinary is it's optical. It uses optical tracking technology.

And there are some tremendous benefits with this. It is the highest precision optical mouse on the market. There are no moving parts. There's no mouse balls to ever clean. There's no performance degradation over time. And you get this optical precision without a mouse pad on almost any surface. So you can farewell mouse pad.

We're really, really happy with this. Now, you may ask, you know, this is really beautiful and there's this continuous surface over the whole thing, where's the button? Oh my God, Apple's gone from a one-button mouse to a no-button mouse.

No, not quite. Because it turns out that this whole continuous surface is the button. The entire surface is the button. It just levers down in the front. It fits any hand, whether it's a child's small hand or an adult's large hand, whether you're right-handed or left-handed. It works with any style. Some people like to click the mouse with just one finger. Some people plop their whole palm on it. It works with any style. And it's got adjustable force, whether you like a delicate button or a slightly heavier push. The entire surface is this beautiful ergonomic button and it works really, really well.

So the new Apple Mouse. Now, this turned out so well. We've been developing this for a while. It turned out so well that we want every Mac owner who uses a mouse to have it. And so we are going to make this new Apple optical mouse standard across our entire desktop line.

It is the first time anyone has ever made an optical mouse standard with a personal computer. And we're going to do it across our entire desktop line. Now, to go with such a great new mouse, we've also designed a new keyboard.

And again, this keyboard responds to some of the requests we've got, because the most popular keyboard in Apple's history was the Apple Extended Keyboard, and we've gone with that layout. We have separate cursor clusters, full-size function keys. We even have volume keys, and there's a key right on the keyboard to eject your disc. So it's really, really nice. And again, we are going to make this standard across our entire desktop line.

Now, if you own a Mac, and you say, "My God, I'd, I'd sure like one of these or both of these," we're going to be selling them as upgrades for only $59 each, and you will be able to buy them on the Apple Store only. We're taking orders today and we'll be delivering them in September. So go ahead and get in the queue, and I think you'll really, really like this.

So, we're going to go from what some people feel is, uh, a, uh, maybe the worst mouse in the industry to what we feel is the best mouse in the industry. And we thought it was so cool that we want to let everyone know, and so we're going to make a TV commercial, and I'd love to show it to you now. Let's go ahead and roll it.

Isn't that great?

All right. So, brand new optical mouse, new pro keyboard, standard on every desktop computer. Now let's get into the computers that they're going to come standard on.

This is our product matrix as you know. So let's start with the Power Mac G4.

Power Mac G4 is an awesome product. Our pro customers love this product. They can get at every component in a few seconds. And of course, it's based on the awesome power of the PowerPC G4 chip. This chip's incredible, and it has something inside it that makes it run even faster called the Velocity Engine. Now the Velocity Engine allows this chip to run at over three and a half gigaflops per second. A gigaflop is a billion instructions per second. How, how fast is that? I mean, it's hard to conceive of what is a gigaflop. Well, let me give you an example. Light travels at about 300 million meters a second, or about 186,000 miles a second. In a billionth of a second, light travels about a foot, right?

When this thing's executing three and a half billion instructions per second, in the time it takes to execute one of those instructions, light travels about 4 inches.

An amusing side note to this is, when you're executing instructions this fast, in the time it takes to execute one instruction, the light which has left your display hasn't even reached your face. That's how fast this is. And we're shipping these chips running at 500 MHz today.

Now you might ask, how does a 500 MHz G4 compare to a 1000 MHz Pentium 3, or what's more commonly known as a gigahertz? How does a 500 MHz G4 stack up against a gigahertz Pentium 3? Well, we'd like to show you right now. And so I'd like to invite Phil Schiller on stage, our Vice President of Worldwide Product Marketing.

We have, we have the best customers in the world. Many of you are here today. And some of our customers do all sorts of graphic things, graphic arts, uh, and one of them is make movie posters. So we can get some great data from some folks that we, uh, work with in Hollywood on some of these great movie posters and it makes for great comparisons in Photoshop. So tell us what we've got here today, Phil.

All right, let's do our shootout. Count us down, Phil.

All right.

Pentium's thinking.

This is the kind of stuff that a lot of our customers do many, many, many times a day. And if they can save a few seconds on each iteration, it amounts to an hour or two a day.

Great. So, what does this tell us? What does this tell us? We have a 500 MHz G4 against a gigahertz Pentium. If you measure the time on these, the Pentium got done in 124 seconds. The G4 completed this task in 100 seconds. And we have dozens of cases like this we could show you if we had enough time this morning. So what does this mean? If you do the math, it means a 500 MHz G4 is as fast as a 1.2 GHz Pentium would be if you could buy one.

Okay? That's what the tests show. And it's pretty amazing. So, we've got ourselves a really, really fast chip here, and it illustrates that it's not just megahertz, it's architecture of the chip and the system that contributes to performance. Megahertz is important, but it's not the only factor as we've just seen here. But you know, we got to thinking, having one really fast processor is great. But you know, two brains are better than one.

What if we could harness the power of two G4 chips at the same time? Well, that's exactly what we're going to do. We have a dual processor G4 here. And I'd like to invite Phil back up to find out how a dual processor G4 runs against a gigahertz Pentium running the same test. Let's roll.

All right.

Now, we could wait for the gigahertz Pentium or not. Uh, why don't we move on?

So, 500 MHz dual processor G4 on that side, gigahertz Pentium 3, and the times, the same 124 seconds by the time the Pentium completes, 61 seconds on the dual processor Power Mac G4.

If you do the math, that is equivalent to a 2 GHz Pentium 3, if you could buy one. You may be able to buy one in 12 to 18 months. We're going to deliver dual processor G4 machines starting today.

We're also running at over 7 gigaflops, 7 billion instructions per second in these machines. So, what are we going to do with this technology? We have three models of Power Mac G4s, all at really attractive prices, 400 MHz, 450 and 500 MHz. Here's what we're going to do. The 400 MHz model will continue to have a single 400 MHz processor in it. The 450 MHz model, however, is going to come standard with two 450 MHz G4s, and the high-end model is going to come standard with two 500 MHz G4 chips. You will not even be able to buy the two high-end models with a single processor. They're going to come standard with dual processors. It is going to be the first personal computers in history to come standard with dual processors.

But we're not done yet. We've got more. On each of these models, on every Power Mac model, we are also adding gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard.

Gigabit Ethernet is the new next generation of Ethernet technology that runs at a gigabit instead of 100 megabits that most systems run at now. This is very expensive stuff if you go add a card into your computer. We are building it onto the motherboard so it doesn't even take a slot. This stuff is really fast and opens up some whole new application areas for our pro customers. So to show us a little bit of that, here's Phil Schiller again.

between the server and the desktop.

Now, my boss has just disconnected the network on me to prove it.
We're on Ethernet.

Pretty cool.

So,

Gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard on all three Power Mac models.
And we're upping the storage as well.
20 gigabytes, 30 gigabytes, and 40 gigabytes built into these products, taking only one of the three drive bays.
So you can expand with two additional drives inside if you want beyond even this.
And of course, our new optical mouse and pro keyboard.
So we're doing all of this.
Dual processor standard on the top two models.
Gigabit Ethernet on the motherboard.
More storage in every model and our new optical mouse and keyboard, and we're doing it all for the same price.

Our teams have worked so hard to be able to throw this stuff in basically without changing prices at all.
We're very happy and all of these models are available today.

So, we have got a really fast chip and a really fast system architecture.
But because two brains are better than one, we're going to make multiprocessing with dual processor standard in the top two Power Mac models, and we think that this is going to be the best Power Mac ever, not only the fastest Macintosh, but continue the Power Max tradition as being the fastest personal computer in the world.

So, now the next thing I'd like to talk about is Mac OS 10.

Mac OS 10 is our new operating system as you may know.
It's rewritten from the ground up.
It's got preemptive multitasking, it's got protected memory, it's got much more modern networking, great plumbing.
It's also got a great new user interface called Aqua, and it also supports what's called symmetric multiprocessing to take full advantage of those dual processors in the new Power Max.
So when you buy one of those new Power Max with dual processors, you're ready for OS 10.
We're on track to ship a public beta of Mac OS 10 in September, I think the very early part of September, and we are on track to release Mac OS 10 very early in 2001, and it's looking great.
And we don't have time to give a full-blown demo today, but I'd like to give you just a demo of the of the user interface in case you've never seen it before.
So let me do that now.

This is Mac OS 10.
And uh a few things very quickly.
I'll just uh launch a document here.
And real quick, as you notice when I move windows around the screen, the whole window moves, not just the outline.
That's also true when I resize things, right?
Really nice.
And um one of the problems we wanted to solve was when you get these dialogues up and you don't know which application or window they're attached to, especially in a true multitasking system.
You may want to go do something else for a while and come back and you have no idea what window that dialogue went with.
Plus you have to manage that dialogue window separately.
So here's what we've done to solve that.
If this is a window, we can say, boom, that's my save panel.
Right on the window.
And so there can be no question which window this is associated with.
And when you're done, boom, it just goes away.
That's simple.
And you may ask, well, what happens if the window is really small?
Well, if the window is really small, it just does this.

And what happens if the window is off screen?
Well, it just does this.
Right?
So everything's been taken care of and now we don't have to manage our dialogues like they are more windows.
I want to show you one other thing about the save panel.
This illustrates some of the philosophy of Mac OS 10.
You've probably never seen a save panel this simple on any computer before.
When you want to save something, you name it and you simply push it this pop-up list that says where.
And in here, it's listed my the desktop, my favorite places, and the recent places I've been.
And I can pick any one of those and save.
Very simple.
But if I want to save somewhere else, I just pop this little control down here and I get a very sophisticated browser here that'll let me go anywhere.
So let's say I want to go into Avi's home directory and save this in Avi's public folder.
I can even add Avi's public folder to my favorites so that the next time, boom, I get this right in here.
I've got Avi's public folder.
So you have complexity when you need it, but we hide it when you don't need it so that the user interface can be much, much simpler.
Next, I'd like to just show you the finder.
The finder is really simple.
There's been some misconceptions about it too.
If you like your hard disk on the desktop, just drag it out.
And uh very easy to just launch a finder by clicking it just like you're used to right now.
We also let you uh show and hide the toolbar.
And uh so I'm going to use it today.
I'll keep it out.
And here's your computer and you can just navigate down here just like you've uh you've done before.
And I can navigate down to my documents as an example.
And as you can see, I don't have to have gritting turned on.
I can put them anywhere I want to, make any kind of a mess that I like.
And but we save you this work because to navigate down to the most popular places because we populate this top with some shortcuts.
So I can get to docs just by clicking this button or apps or my favorites or my home or other users or the computer.
And it's very, very easy uh to move around.
Now, I also have different views on things.
I have icon view, I have list view, and I have a new browser view.
And I can click back and forth between them with this little control on every finder window.
So we know what icon and list view are, but you may not have seen browser view before.
Browser view is very simple.
It lets me start anywhere and just browse along these columns.
So I'll pick in my home directory, pick my documents, and uh I can pick one.
I even have a preview mode.
And I can see exactly where I've been.
I can click anywhere back there to go back and I've got a little previewer here for things.
I can even preview uh movies if I want to, you know.

[Music]

I can uh even have QuickTime VR previews, you know, if I want.
And uh I can even preview MP3s if I want to, you know.

[Music]

You get the idea.
Now, the next thing I'd like to show you is the dock.

The dock is wonderful.
It's a place to put those apps you use the most, those documents you use the most, and miniaturize windows.
So this is the dock and anyone can change the size of the dock to anything that suits them.
They can have it small, they can have it big.
And when you put more things in the dock, it just shrinks to fit.
So let me go back as an example to add an application.
I can add an application like an image capture app anywhere in here.
Just drop it down and boom, the dock shrinks.
And I can move things around in the dock, change any order that I might like.
I can also add a bunch of apps at one time if I choose to.
I can add all these apps and again, you can see the dock shrink a little bit more.
These are just links.
So when I'm done using this app, I can just drag these out and it just breaks the link, very simple.

No problema.
Uh I can also add documents in the dock and it solves an age-old problem on the Macintosh, which is miniaturization.
When you're working on something and you want to go work on something else for a little while and get it out of the way, right now our miniaturization, this window shade thing, doesn't really get it out of the way.
It leaves this big window shade on your desk.
So what we've built in is the following.
You just miniaturize a window and boom, it's right there with its thumbnail automatically built for you.
Let me show you this in slow motion.
It's kind of fun to watch.
Just the craftsmanship that the team has built into this is amazing.
Isn't that nice?

Watch this.
Even if it's down here, watch what it does.

Isn't that nice?
So you always know where something's coming from and where it's going to, and you have these at your disposal uh right in the dock and just click on them and boom, they're back where you left them.
Now, I'd like to show you one last thing.
Uh let me bring up a QuickTime file, the Mission Impossible trailer.
And uh we can go ahead and uh play it here.

[Movie Trailer]

Agent.
Okay.
So uh let me show you something.
Look at this.
I put it in slow-mo here.
Isn't that cool?

[Movie Trailer]

So uh one last thing.
I'll show you uh one of the wonderful benefits of Mac OS 10.
We've got this app we wrote called the bomb app and the bomb app does everything it can to crash the system.
It rewrites low memory, it does all the nasty things that programmers are never supposed to do.
I apologize in advance for this application.

[Movie Trailer]

And this app did pretty cool.

So a brief overview of Mac OS 10.
All righty.
Now, we've been working with a lot of our developer partners very closely, but none more closely than Adobe.
Adobe's right down the block from us.
We have a fantastic relationship with them and I'd like to invite Bruce Chizen, the president of Adobe up on stage to say a few words.
Bruce.

Thanks Steve.
How you doing?
So it's clear from the Photoshop demo that we do work really closely with Apple.
We have hundreds of engineers that are working with them on getting our applications over to OS 10.
They are extremely impressed and we are absolutely committed to putting those apps, all of those key apps.
Um so as Apple rolls out OS 10, Adobe will be there.
Many of you are Adobe customers and you're using applications like InDesign, Go Live, Premiere, After Effects, and of course Photoshop to create compelling websites, print publications, videos.
The challenge is you're working with extremely large files, large and complex files.
And you need those files to be manipulated quickly.
Well, you need a quick system.
And now we have the ultimate system to create those compelling websites and that is the new G4 MP.
It is truly the ultimate Photoshop machine.
So Steve, thanks.
I can't wait to get my hands on one.

Thank you, Bruce.
Get him one.
Okay, so that's Mac OS 10.
Now, next, I'd like to talk about another partner that we work very closely with, and that's Microsoft.
Our relationship with Microsoft has been getting better and better.
We've been working with them very closely on another major new product for Mac customers, and that is the new version of Office for Macintosh, Microsoft Office 2001.
It looks terrific and to show it to us, I'd like to uh bring up Kevin Brown, the general manager of the Macintosh business unit at Microsoft.

Five or 10 minutes on homepage builder and add that quick time movie to your personal website which is hosted by Apple 24x7 at no charge and anyone can access it.
Pretty amazing.

Today, we've talked about a lot of things.
New Power Mac G4s with dual processors as standard in the top two models, as fast as a theoretical 2 gigahertz Pentium.
We've talked about new iMacs in stunning new colors, aggressive new price points, amazing new features.
We've talked about Mac OS 10 coming soon, Microsoft Office 2001 coming soon, all the Bungie games continuing to come to the Mac, iMovie 2 and homepage builder.
That's a lot for one day.
But there's one more thing.

This is our product strategy that we announced about two and a half years ago, the four quadrants.
And it's served us very well.
We've filled them all in and we've even had a chance to go around and update most of them two or three times each to constantly keep them fresh and aggressive.
But today, the first time in two and a half years, we are expanding our product strategy.
And it's not a portable.
It is a new desktop machine.
What is it?

We are combining the power of the Power Mac G4, the awesome power of this machine with the desktop elegance, the silence and the miniaturization that we learned from doing the iMacs to make a whole new class of machine.
And so, we're starting with the G4 power, we're building in a really fast G4 chip into this new machine.
We're building in the ability to have up to a gigabyte and a half of memory in the machine.
We're building in the ability to have up to 40 gigabytes of storage inside the machine.
We're adding IO for everything, modem, 100 megabit per second Ethernet, USB and firewire.
You can hook up to almost anything with this machine.
And airport wireless networking inside as well.
Now, I know some of you are saying, well, looks like a mid-range Power Mac G4 to me.
What's so new and special about this?
Well, this is where we get into the iMac magic.
Because if this is the size of a Power Mac G4, we have miniaturized all that power into something this size.
Okay?
From this to this.
And what we've miniaturized it into is an 8 inch cube.
An 8 inch cube.
Unbelievable.
Another way of looking at this is, if this is the Power Mac G4 and you could break it into four equal parts, we have miniaturized all the power into just one of those parts, which is an 8 inch cube.
Unbelievable.
Now, you can imagine with all this power in such a dense space, we must need a turbo fan to cool this thing.
But no.
Our engineers have done some brilliant work and all this power in an 8 inch cube has cooled without a fan.
And so, it runs in virtual silence in an 8 inch cube.
And we call this new product the Power Mac G4 Cube or more affectionately the G4 Cube.
And I would like to show it to you now.
Let's bring it out.

This is a stunning product, quite possibly the most beautiful product we've ever designed.
The computer is in an 8 inch cube and it's suspended in a stunning crystal clear enclosure.
There's also a slot load DVD drive, but where is it you ask?

That cool?
Wish you didn't see it?
So everything is in there, very conveniently located to sit right next to you on your desk.
Now, our engineers spent an enormous amount of energy figuring out how to get this amazingly powerful G4 technology into this 8 inch cube and to cool it without a fan.
But they also spent enormous amount of time figuring out how to get it out quickly.
Because our pro customers like to get at every component in a system within a matter of a few seconds.
So here's what we did.
You can take your Power Mac G4 and simply turn it over.
Right?
Let's get the video here.
I want you to see this.
You push down on this handle and it pops up and you literally lift all of the technology out.

You have access.
You have access to every single component.
And when you're done, you just put it back in, pop down the handle to lock it in.
We even have a Kensington lock to make sure you're the only one that opens your G4 cube.
Pop it right back over and you're in business.
Pretty nice.

So, the G4 Cube.
It's amazing.
DVD drive in the top.
Amazing cooling system through a center channel that cools the whole thing with air so that it runs in virtual silence.
The G4 Cube.
And again, a size comparison with the Power Mac shows how small it really is.
And just like the Power Mac allows you to access any component in seconds, so does the G4 Cube allow you to get at every component in just seconds.
We're very, very proud of this.
But we didn't stop there.
We designed a whole system.
And so we've worked with Harman Kardon to design a pair of Apple design stereo speakers that are gorgeous.
And obviously our new optical mouse and pro keyboard comes with the system as well.
And the system is really beautiful.
And for a system like this that's configured with a 450 MHz G4, 64 meg memory, 20 gigabytes of storage, slot load DVD drive, firewire and iMovie, for this whole system, $17.99.

And we have a second model that features a 500 MHz G4 processor, 128 megabytes of memory, 30 gigs of hard storage, DVD ROM, firewire, iMovie, make the ultimate iMovie machine.
And it's available for $22.99 and this is an Apple online store exclusive.
So you can just go to the Apple online store and order this.
All models are available in early August, just a few weeks away.
Power Mac G4 Cube.
We are so proud of this thing.
It is a complete system in every way.
Except for displays.
Oh yeah.
We have three new displays we're introducing today.
We'd like to bring them out now.
They are in equally stunning designs.

The first, a new CRT display.
It's a 17-inch Diamondtron display that's naturally flat on the front.
It's totally flat and as you can see, you can see all the way through it in the back.
It's really stunning.
And it's got this good stand on it as well that's very beautiful.
It's got two USB ports built into the display.
So you can plug your keyboard into the display.
You don't have to have cables going back to the computer.
It's got color sync built in.
We calibrated it at the factory, it stays calibrated through the life of the display.
And maybe the coolest thing.
You know how you have a lot of cable clutter on your desk with all sorts of power cables and other kinds of cables?
Well, this display is powered from the computer.
One cable carries video, USB and power from the computer.
So there's only one cable replacing three.

And $499.
Next display.
A 15-inch flat LCD.
It's really beautiful.
It's a perfect companion to the G4 Cube.
It's got 1024x768 resolution.
Again, two USB ports.
It's got touch controls on it to bring up the display controls or even to put your system to sleep and wake it up.
And it is powered from the computer with one cable just like the other.
$999.
Very aggressive.
Makes a beautiful companion to the new G4 Cube.
And our cinema display, we have a new cinema display that's enhanced to again be powered from the computer with only one cable carrying USB, video and power over the one cable.
All three of these displays go on sale today and all three of them work not only with the G4 Cube but with the Power Mac as well.
So three new displays.
We've got a video we'd like to show you about this amazing new system.
So let's roll it.

We've been working on this for a long time and it's so great to be able to tell you about it today.
The new Power Mac G4 Cube takes its place in an expanded product line.
And if you've noticed, all three of our desktop product lines which constitute over 75% of our unit volume are all new as of today.

It's amazing.
And I would like, you know, it is, it is a privilege to be able to be on the same team as the talented people at Apple.
These people are not only so talented, but they're emotional.
They're passionate and they love, they put love into these products.
And I hope you can see that today.
And I'd like all the Apple folks in the audience to stand up and all the folks on the satellite feed back in Cupertino and the other sites to stand up, please.
Let's give them a round of applause.

I don't think there's another team on the planet that could be creating products like this.
So, thank you for coming today.
We've had a lot.
And I started with the mouse.
I'd like to end with the mouse.
This optical mouse is the symbol of all the new products today for me.
It comes with all the new products that you saw and it's also just a better way of doing things, not doing things the same old way but innovating.
And it came out so wonderful that not only are we going to bundle it with all our desktop computers, but I want all of you to be the first ones to get your hands on it.
And so we're going to give you one today.

As you, as you leave the auditorium, as you leave the auditorium, if you have one of these tickets, you will be handed a new Apple optical mouse and in just a second you'll find that you can get one of these tickets under your seats.
So thank you very much for coming today.
We've enjoyed showing you all our new stuff.

From this to this.

An 8 inch cube.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

Wish you didn't see it?

It's amazing.
DVD drive in the top.
Amazing cooling system through a center channel that cools the whole thing with air so that it runs in virtual silence.
The G4 Cube.

Power Mac G4 Cube.
We are so proud of this thing.
It is a complete system in every way.
Except for displays.
Oh yeah.

$999.
Very aggressive.
Makes a beautiful companion to the new G4 Cube.
And our cinema display, we have a new cinema display that's enhanced to again be powered from the computer with only one cable carrying USB, video and power over the one cable.
All three of these displays go on sale today and all three of them work not only with the G4 Cube but with the Power Mac as well.
So three new displays.
We've got a video we'd like to show you about this amazing new system.
So let's roll it.

**[Steve Jobs]**: We've been working on this for a long time and it's so great to be able to tell you about it today.
The new Power Mac G4 Cube takes its place in an expanded product line.
And if you've noticed, all three of our desktop product lines which constitute over 75% of our unit volume are all new as of today.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: It's amazing.

This optical mouse is the symbol of all the new products today for me.

**[Audience]**: [Applause]

**[Steve Jobs]**: As you, as you leave the auditorium, as you leave the auditorium, if you have one of these tickets, you will be handed a new Apple optical mouse and in just a second you'll find that you can get one of these tickets under your seats.

documents.title: WWDC 2003
documents.speaker: Steve Jobs
documents.content:
Good morning.

Good morning. Thank you.

Isn't it great to be in San Francisco?

So, we have so much great stuff for you today that we may even have to take a stretch break in the middle here.

A lot of good stuff. I hope you love it uh as much as we do. So, there are about 3800 of us here today. Uh we're a little over 1% of the registered Apple developers. There's over 300,000 now and that number has tripled since the num- since the introduction of Mac OS 10. Uh not only carbon and cocoa developers but a ton of Unix developers have joined us, a lot of Java developers as well. So, we're really excited about this.

I want to start with some updates and then we'll get into the meat of today's presentation. First, I want to talk about Airport Extreme. Uh Airport Extreme is our 54 megabit per second airport product that's based on the industry standard 802.11g. And the standard was not yet ratified when we started shipping in January. We were the first to ship this, but it was ratified uh a little over a week ago. And one week after it was ratified, we had an airport soft- software update on the net for base stations and cards to bring them totally in compliance with the final ratified spec. We are 1000% sure that 802.11g is the successor to 802.11b. It's totally backwards compatible. And as I mentioned, Apple was the first to ship 802.11g in our industry just as we were the first to ship uh 802.11 wireless networking in computers years ago. And I'm pleased to report that since we started shipping 802.11g in January, we've shipped over 300,000 802.11g products. So that's an update on Airport Extreme. We couldn't be happier with the progress. Next, I want to give you an update on our retail stores. Uh this is off the charts. Uh it's been 25 months since we opened our first store. We now have 58 stores open. Since we've opened them, we've had over 17 million visitors to our stores. 17 million. This is our store in New York. It's one of the coolest stores in New York. If you've ever been there, I'd worth a visit if you're in the city. It's wonderful. This is our largest store in Los Angeles in the Grove Shopping Center and again shows how much software we carry in our stores. We love to carry your software. And among the many stores we're going to be opening in the next year, we're opening three really great stores, one in Chicago, one in San Francisco and one in Tokyo. We're opening Chicago this coming weekend.

And this is a photo from last week.

This is right on Michigan Avenue, which is the uh best shopping street in America outside of Fifth Avenue in New York. It's phenomenal. That big Apple logo in the middle is actually a window uh that you can see right in, get some natural light in the second floor. In San Francisco, we don't have anything constructed yet. We'll open San Francisco uh next spring. But uh this is a rendering. I wish it was as easy to build them. Uh and uh this is at the end of Stockton Street viewed from Market Street. This is what it will look like, only a few blocks from where we are sitting here right now. And in Tokyo, we are opening a store.

It's going to be great. In Tokyo, we are opening a store on the Ginza uh which is the number one shopping street in the world and we're opening it early next year and again this is a rendering of what it will be.

So, we've had 17 million visitors and counting. We love to sell your software and hardware accessory products. So keep keep feeding them to us and we can't wait to put them in our stores. So that's an update on our retail stores. Next, iPod. iPod, again, we couldn't be happier with. We just introduced our third generation iPod. Our competitors haven't even caught up with our first generation yet. We're in our third and it is amazing. Uh it is as light as two CDs in their jewel cases. It is as thin as two CD jewel cases back to back. It has a dock so that charging and sinking is even more convenient than before. And I've got a great milestone today. Today's an auspicious day because later on today we will ship our 1 millionth iPod.

So, another great product for music of course, iTunes 4. And the greatest feature of iTunes 4 is of course the iTunes Music Store. Being an auspicious day today, it was eight weeks ago today that we launched the iTunes Music Store, only eight weeks ago and I'm pleased to report that in the first eight weeks, we've sold over 5 million songs online.

We crossed the 5 million mark this last Saturday and we again are thrilled. Now, we ran an ad campaign about uh about the iTunes Music Store and you know when you run an ad campaign if it's really working, if it if it resonates with the culture, if people start to parody it. And uh it wasn't very long before that happened and uh when I saw this on on TV.

So, doesn't get any better than that. Okay, so that's the iTunes Music Store. Next, I want to give you an update on Safari. As you know, Safari is the fastest browser on the Mac and we think it's the best browser on any platform. We've had over 5 million downloads of the Safari beta software that we released in January and it's a phenomenal browser. We were able over the course of the beta period to add tab browsing. I think we've got the slickest implementation of tab browsing ever done. It's been six months that we've had the beta software out there. You guys have given us a phenomenal number of comments. We've incorporated as many as we could in and I think we've got an incredibly solid browser now. And so today we are declaring Safari 1.0.

We're releasing it on the web in a few hours. You can download your copy and we're also fulfilling a request we've had from so many of you that want to embed Safari functionality in your apps by just calling a few carbon or cocoa APIs. Today we're releasing a Safari SDK to all of you as well.

So, that's Safari and that concludes my updates. Now let's get right into it. I want to talk about Mac OS 10. Mac OS 10 is doing really, really well. Let me show you. Over the last two years, we've gone from about a half a million active users to 7 million active users of Mac OS 10. And look at the slope of that curve. It's going up. We have 6,000 native Mac OS 10 apps. And again, let's take a look at the slope of this curve over the last two years starting with under 1000. It's accelerating. And this is obviously these two are linked. And so we are over the crest of the hill of the Mac OS 10 transition and we'll finish it up this year. And all I can say for all these apps is thank you. I know this has been a lot of work for some of you as any major OS transition is and you guys have really come through and we are just about through with this and we've got a kickass OS. So thank you.

But today, for all of us in this room, all the developers, Jaguar is over.

Because today we're going to preview Panther for you. The next major release of Mac OS 10, version 10.3. Its name is Panther and it's the fourth major release of Mac OS 10 following Cheetah, Puma and Jaguar. In Panther, there are over 100 major new features. We're not going to have time to go over all of them today, but I want to cover a few of them with you and I think you'll agree it's a stunning release. First, let's start off with Unix. As you know, Mac OS 10 is Unix based and as you also know, Mac OS 10 is now the most popular Unix in the world. The most popular Unix in the world. And we've enhanced it for Panther. We got a lot of cool new features. X11 is bundled in, NFS file locking, much faster Unix file system, much more robust Kerberos, Free BSD 5.0, IPv6 and a lot of popular Unix APIs that you guys have asked for. All of that and a lot more Unix stuff is in Panther. Now, in addition to Unix though, we support the other guys too. We want to help our customers work in heterogeneous networks and we've added a lot of stuff for Windows operability. We're shipping the latest version of Samba that just came out. We're the first folks to ship that I believe so that you can now browse SMB servers dynamically right in the finder, SMB printing, you can put your home directories on SMB servers. We're shipping a new IPsec based VPN, which is the new standard for VPN adopted by Cisco and Microsoft and us and a lot deeper active directory integration. So, a lot of stuff with Windows interoperability. Now let's get into some of the cooler stuff. Panther has a brand new finder.

Now, you might say, well wait a minute, what was wrong with the old finder? Well, the old finder was computer centric. When we really were honest with ourselves, we had to admit it. We did as best as we could, but we didn't quite get across the goal line. It was computer centric. What do I mean by that? Well, this is column view in the old finder, the Jaguar finder and that's my stuff right there, right? That's my stuff. Four levels down. How could I be the most important thing if I'm four levels down? And I need stuff at other levels and it's just very confusing. So, we want to replace this computer centric finder with a user centric finder. Well, how do we do that? Well, we start off by learning from some of the other interfaces we've built over the last few years and we said let's put all the stuff you want including stuff you want to drag in in one column and put it on the left and that's what we've done. All your storage, your removable storage, your iDisk, your home directory, any folders you want in one column. And let's put that on the left of a window. This might look a little bit like playlists in iTunes or photo albums in iPhoto. That's because it is. And you click on one of these things and boom, your stuff is right there. So here's my home, here's my applications, here's my documents. I can look at these things in column view, list view or icon view and have my stuff right there. Boom. And I can drag any folders I want right into that left column. It's really, really simple. Now, we've done more. We've added fast searching. So you can now search for files really fast and find them. We've added a thing called the action button. We found a lot of our users never found some of the cool things they could do. Some of them didn't even find get info. And so we pulled all that stuff under a button that's contextually sensitive. You push it, it'll show you exactly what you can do with a document or folder that you have selected. We've added labels. We got a lot of requests for labels. They're in there. As I mentioned earlier, we have dynamic network browsing. So you can dynamically search for Unix servers, for Windows servers, for any servers right from the finder. We've got new open and save panels that reflect this more user centric point of view, much cleaner. And probably the best way is for me to show this to you now.

So, the new finder. Here we go. You see the left column right here? I can just click down it and see all my stuff. And uh I can go ahead and go into icon view again. Just bop around and see all of my stuff very easy. And I can shrink the window. There's a lot of fit and finish on this so you'll notice the icons on the left shrink, right? Just like this. Don't scroll till they have to. And I can drag stuff in. I can drag a folder I want anywhere in here if I want to, just put it right there. And I click on that and I see its contents. If I'm tired of it, I just drag it out and it poofs. Okay. I can eject DVDs right from here with a roll over right like this so I don't even have to go to an eject button. And I can go on the network and see my servers right here and browse them dynamically. Now, let me go to my documents folder and uh oh maybe uh where is it? Boom boom boom. I can go pick the action menu and again, I can label something right like this. And boom, that's all it does. All it takes to set a label. It's very, very simple. And I've got fast search. So I'm in my home directory now. I can search all my my hard disks or just my home directory or window it down to whatever I want. I'm going to look for all the Xserve uh documents in my home directory just by typing Xserve. So the minute I start to type,

Pretty cool, huh? And I'll keep going. Uh I'll refine that to type in raid and boom, there's my Xserve documents raid. I can even type in uh extensions if I want to and find all those. I can find all the iMac documents. Boom. Or eMac documents or PowerBook documents. Boom. It's that fast. It's really, really cool. And so that's a brief overview of the new finder and uh I think you're going to like it a lot. We've got it's user centric. We've got fast searching. We've got the action button to pull together a lot of commands that people have never found, labels, dynamic network browsing and new open and save panels that reflect the new user centric sensibility. So this is the new finder and I think uh it's going to serve us well. I think we finally got there on the finder with something that's the best the world's ever seen. Next is iDisk. We've enhanced iDisk significantly for Panther. Uh iDisk as you know is for our .Mac customers, the hundreds of thousands of people that have signed up for .Mac and iDisk has been a place where you can manually upload files to the .Mac server and manually download them. Well, that's all changing in Panther because in Panther we're automatically syncing the files. And what that means is is that stuff that's on your iDisk will automatically sync with our servers on .Mac in both directions. And it does it in the background. So what it really means is your iDisk becomes basically a local folder that syncs. You don't put stuff in your iDisk to send it up to .Mac. You leave it in your iDisk. You can leave a document in your iDisk, open it up, modify it, close it and the minute you close it, it will sync back up to .Mac in the background automatically. So you can just leave stuff in your iDisk. And this is pretty cool. It's a great way to back stuff up. But in addition to that, it really shines when you have untethered portables. You can be out in the field not connected to a network, change a document in your iDisk. The minute you're connected to a network whether you walk into an airport, a base station or you hook back up to a terrestrial net, boom, that document that's changed will automatically sync with .Mac. It's really nice and that is the new iDisk in Panther. Next up, we have a new feature called Exposé. What is Exposé? Well, we've made it so wonderful to use multiple apps at once that people do, right? The operating system is so bulletproof that if an app crashes it doesn't crash the system and we have such beautiful uh multitasking that you can have, you know, seven, eight, nine, 10 apps open at once. I'm sure most of you do. So you've got Photoshop shop open and you're working on a bunch of Photoshop images. You've got mail open, you've got your browser open, you've got your address book open and what do you end up with this? Right? We've all been there. We all are there several times a day and you want to find that one window you're looking for. How do you do it? All you want is to bring the one window you want to the front. So you move everything out of the way. You're like a you're on a scavenger hunt. Well, we figured out how to solve this in a wonderful way. Let me show you now.

I'm going to start off by opening a lot of uh applications and I'm just going to run a little Apple script to do that for me. It's going to open mail.

It's opening some Photoshop documents here. Few browser windows. All right. So I think that's that's probably about done. We got a lot of stuff open here and uh you know, a lot of Photoshop windows, Photoshop palettes. How do I find something? Well, here's how we do it. You ready? Oh, just like this.

Let me uh let me show you this in slow mo. And as you notice, as I mouse around here, it shows me exactly what the windows are. Boom, right? Boom, boom, boom, boom. Now, let's say I just want to see my Photoshop windows or one application's windows. Well, I select that application and I do this. Again, just the one app's windows. Notice the

---

## Part 2

the pallets fade away. The other apps highlight and dim out in the background, or I can go see all of them just like this. It's very, very nice. Let me show you this again in slow mo here.

We think that's about to go up. Because in Panther, we are taking iChat to iChat AV. The A stands for audio, the V stands for video. iChat AV goes beyond just text chats and to the instant messaging infrastructure adds audio chats over the internet and video chats. It's remarkable. It is video conferencing for the rest of us. It is one of the coolest things we've ever done. And we realized that video chat, video conferencing was really just the ultimate instant messaging. And so we built it right into that wonderful infrastructure and you can access it right from your buddy list. Right from the buddy list. So we have now text, audio, and video chats. Zero setup or configuration. Zero. You literally plug in the camera and everything else is done automatically. You don't have to know if your buddy has a camera or a setup for audio conferencing, it figures it out and shows you right on your buddy list what they're set up for. There is zero setup or configuration. There are no phone numbers or IP addresses to type in. This all works off the instant messaging infrastructure, so all you have to have is their buddy name. That's it. No matter where they are. It is location independent. As I travel around and connect to the network, I'm automatically telling the instant messaging server where I am. And so you as a sender to me know exactly where I am. You don't have to know. And if I'm going to call somebody, I got a pretty good idea if they're there because instant messaging provides presence as well. So we're leveraging the entire instant messaging infrastructure. It's not like making a phone call where I got to know, you know, you've got a work, a home, and a mobile number. I got to call each one and you might not be at any of them. Right? Or you might have changed them. We don't have to worry about any of that with instant messaging because the infrastructure handles it all. Wherever you are, all I have to do is click on your name and boom, we're connected. And you can get a buddy name, you can get a free AIM name from AOL, you can get a free .mac buddy name from Apple, or you can use your Rendezvous buddy list and just connect with the people around you on an ad hoc basis. iChat AV works with any FireWire camera, built-in or USB microphones. You can even use camcorders if you have one. It's really amazing. You need a modem. A 56k modem is all you need for audio chats. Free long distance phone calls over the net if you've got an ISP connection. It's amazing. And you need broadband for video conferencing. And that means DSL, cable, T1, or Ethernet. But you know what? A whole lot of people have this now. Every business has broadband. Most schools in this country have broadband. Many hotels now have Ethernet jacks right in the rooms. And over 25 million homes have broadband. A lot of people have broadband and we think this is really ripe to take off. This is video conferencing for the rest of us. And we've waited a long time to show you this, but I'd like to show you.

Now, my friend and yours, Phil Schiller, uh, is in the back room. And we're connecting to AIM right now. Got this stuff here. And, uh, I'm going to go ahead and call Phil. And the way I call Phil is, uh, I just go over to my buddy list and there he is and I can pick his name and pick this little camera down here. I can just click the camera right next to his picture. I click the camera and I get a little preview here, right there.

Hi, Phil.

How you doing?

Hey, listen, I'm sorry you couldn't be out on stage with me, but, uh, we wanted to put you in like a home setting or something like that. Look, I can just stretch this out here, anything I want. Tell us something, Phil.

And we can even make this full screen. Look at this.

You know, we've been using this, a few of us have been using this internally at Apple for over a month now and this has completely changed the way that we work. I can call Phil up now 11:00 at night and see him.

Well, listen, Phil, I will, uh, I will talk to you later. Uh, thank you very much for being the, uh, first public, uh, video conference we've ever done with iChat AV.

Now, what about the future? We're at 2 GHz today. IBM and Apple are today announcing that within 12 months, we'll be at 3 GHz. 3 GHz processor clock, that's up 50% within 12 months. And so believe me, this architecture has legs. Power Mac G5, an amazing, amazing new machine. And we've got a video that I'd like to show you now. So let's run the video.
Today's personal computers use 32-bit technology.
The computers of the future will use 64-bit. Well, the future is now at Apple. Check it out my new weapon. What a choice. The new Power Mac G5 is the world's first personal computer with a 64-bit processor, accelerating everything from 3D animation to scientific computation. Oh boy, this is going to be good, I can tell. When we started the G5, we knew we couldn't make something just a little bit faster. We had to make it a whole lot faster and we did. In fact, it's the world's most powerful personal computer, period. This new Power Mac G5 has bandwidth to burn. Dual 2 GHz 64-bit Power PC processor with optimized velocity engines. Dual GHz processor buses, each capable of transferring up to 8 GB per second. A memory sub system that supports up to 8 GB of 400 MHz DDR RAM with 6.4 GB per second of bandwidth. The new Power Mac G5 has blazingly fast expansion, the fastest ever in a personal computer. It features state-of-the-art 8X AGP Pro graphics, 133 MHz PCI-X slots for cutting edge music and video solutions and two serial ATA buses for ultra fast internal storage. The Power Mac is completely new from the ground up. At its heart is a Power PC G5 processor, which can handle over 200 in-flight instructions. That's 70% more than the fastest Pentium on the market today. To create this processor, we turned to IBM. The goal of this partnership is for Apple and IBM to come together so that Apple customers get the best of both worlds, the tremendous creativity from the Apple Corporation and the tremendous technology from the IBM Corporation. IBM invested over $3 billion in a new fab to produce these large 300 mm wafers. This G5 microprocessor has over 50 million transistors on it and it incorporates IBM's leading edge 130 nanometer technology. That's 1 800th the diameter of a human hair, but this is only the beginning. We have already built the prototypes for next generation Power PC microprocessors.
The G5 is an incredibly fast chip and it's so fast, so powerful that it requires extraordinary cooling. We've designed the new Power Mac G5 with four distinct thermal zones. Now, with thermal sensors in each zone, we can actually cool them independently. And that's important because it means we can cool them quietly. In fact, it's two to three times quieter than the G4. What a choice. Everything is designed to be straightforward. The door is removable, which allows you complete access to the hard drive, to cards, and to the RAM. The Power Mac G5 is an amazing feat of engineering, featuring two incredibly fast Power PC processors, up to 500 GB of internal storage, a super drive, up to 8 GB of memory, breaking the 4 GB barrier. Everything and more that you'd expect from Apple's top of the line machine.

After running our Renderman benchmark, we can now say that the G5 is the fastest desktop in the world. I think the one word that describes the Power Mac G5 to me is stunning. It's stunning because while people have speculated that Apple might change chips, they had no idea about this entire redesign of the architecture. It's stunning. The beautiful thing about the G5's ability to run 32-bit and 64-bit programs natively is that artists like to use lots of different programs. Well, they don't have to worry about compatibility with their old programs and their new programs. They're just going to work and they're going to work faster. My first reaction to the G5 was just one of wow. Apple has done it again. The performance of the G5 is just incredible. We've been working very closely with Apple, in particular with Adobe Photoshop. In fact, it's up to two times as fast as the previous performance that we've experienced on the Macintosh. Apple's made Photoshop that much more productive. The G5 is faster than any Unix workstation. It runs all of your desktop software, all of your productivity applications. It runs Mathematica version 5 incredibly well. And the real question is, why would you buy anything else?
The new G5 is the most advanced personal computer in the world. And in partnership with IBM, we're committed to seeing that it remains the most advanced for years to come. From the processors to the buses to the memory, this is one kickass machine.

Well, let's just go back less than six months ago, the beginning of the year, the 12-inch PowerBook, the smallest footprint, lightest full featured notebook in the world. The 17-inch PowerBook, the world's first 17-inch notebook computer, still the only 17-inch notebook computer, 1 inch thin.
